TITLE: Study reveals the scope of prehistoric violence in the Middle East
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-13T09:16:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/archaeology/2023-10-13/ty-article/study-reveals-the-scope-of-prehistoric-violence-in-the-middle-east/0000018b-2416-d3fc-a3bf-bfffeddc0000

Just how innately brutal are humans? From the start of the historic record about 4,500 years ago, the narratives abound in violence. But the historic record began thousands of years after a radical change in the human condition: For the first time in two million years, we had settled down. Were we potentially friendlier in prehistory?
We don’t know, as prehistoric osteological evidence is scarce. But some evidence remains. Archaeologists suspect they may have discovered the murder of a Neanderthal by a Homo sapiens who shivved him in the ribcage. A battlefield from over 13,000 years ago has been found in Sudan, featuring weapons that archaeologists suspect were designed to lacerate and maim rather than kill efficiently. The remains of a slaughter from 10,000 years ago have been found in Kenya.
Cave paintings representing weapons usually depict hunting, but some prehistoric art in the Sahara Desert (at Sefar in Algeria) and Spain (at Les Dogues) seem to show fierce combat between groups of archers, possibly including a battle between two groups of women.
But these are isolated examples. Now, a paper published this week in Nature Human Behavior focusing on the Middle East presents, for the first time, a bird’s-eye view of trends in violence from 14,000 to 2,400 years ago, between the end of the Ice Age (the Mesolithic) and Classical Antiquity.
To try to discern trends, the researchers constructed and analyzed a dataset based on 3,539 skeletons unearthed in seven Middle Eastern countries: Turkey, Israel, Iraq, Iran, Syria, Lebanon, and Jordan. To quantify the intensity of interpersonal violence, they used the proportion of bodies with weapon-related wounds or cranial trauma injuries.
Why focus on the Middle East? Because this region was always a hotbed of societal evolution. Settlement seems to have begun at least 23,000 years ago, and would be followed by profound transformations. These ranged from hunting to animal domestication and from foraging to farming as of about 10,000 years ago. The Chalcolithic brought the urban revolution, the rise of agrarian states, and their evolution into aggressive empires.
What the team found is more nuanced than the crude paradigm of “hawk” and “dove.” Violence seems to have fluctuated, Joerg Baten of the University of Tübingen, Giacomo Benati of the University of Barcelona, and Arkadiusz Soltysiak of the University of Warsaw deduced. Amid these fluctuations, the researchers detect spikes in violence in the late Chalcolithic Age, 6,500 years ago, and again in the Late Bronze Age, about 3,500 years ago. What changed to trigger these lethal surges?
Hawks and doves
Some researchers believe hunter-gatherers were mostly peaceful, turning belligerent mainly after the advent of settlement. There is also a hawkish hypothesis that we have always been pugnacious but that the long-term trend of violence has declined over the millennia, especially since the so-called Age of Enlightenment.
There is disagreement over the rigors and uncertainties of prehistoric hunting-gathering society against those of early agrarian life. Currently, it is thought that the respective travails of hunter-gatherers and farmers, and the relative benefits of their lifestyles, depended on their specific circumstances.
Of course, the historical record is rife with violence, from the earliest manuscripts of Mesopotamia to Classical Antiquity and Biblical times. But we shouldn’t necessarily project that onto prehistory, because the dovish hypothesis suggests that population density was low during the epochs of hunting and gathering.
That means prehistoric hunter-gatherers didn’t need to wrangle; not tied to property they needed to defend, they could move along when things went pear-shaped. This hypothesis suggests that aggression began to mount as cities and proto-states emerged during the Chalcolithic, increasing population density and with it, stress.
In Israel, a new population arrived from Turkey and Iran in the Chalcolithic, 6,500 years ago, bringing with them a new style of exquisite pottery and, it seems, blue eyes.
Following the mayhem of the Chalcolithic, interpersonal violence ebbed during the Early Bronze Age. This may have been because of the synergetic effect of the development of states, laws, and trade. Then came the Late Bronze Age; a terrible, 300-year drought struck and the great civilizations around the Mediterranean imploded in another surge in violence.
This is the hypothesis. How well does that fit with empirical findings? Pretty well, given the spikes in violence that the data indicates in the Chalcolithic and Late Bronze Age.
The nature of the beast
Advocates of humanity’s hawkishness can point to history. Note, however, that likely only a fragment of the entire ancient body of writing has survived, and it’s bloody.
Proto-writing in the Middle East (as opposed to Asia) goes back almost 7,000 year. It apparently arose because of administrative needs. The earliest examples seem to be “tags” saying things like (for instance) “Goat, Farhad, two.” Then came inventories, receipts, letters, and customer complaints.
We don’t know when texts extolling the wonders of this or that deity or leader began to be written. the earliest known example from the region is the roughly 4,000-year-old epic poem about King Gilgamesh of Uruk, apparently a real person who reigned about 4,700 years ago. The story of Gilgamesh involves more than a little bloodshed. Perhaps not coincidentally, the earliest known record of war, between the Sumerians and the Elamites, comes from around 4,700 years ago in Mesopotamia.
From somewhat later, the Bible brims with descriptions of terrible hostilities, as do so many ancient texts.
Where this violence came from, and whether it goes back to deep prehistory, has never been clear. It still isn’t quite, but the study authors have put together whatever information they could.
The war in prehistoric Sudan is the earliest known battlefield identified by archaeologists. Taking place 13,000 years ago, it was within the timeframe of the researchers’ paper, but outside it geographically.
Ultimately, the data indicates a clear increase in violence starting 14,000 years ago and peaking in the Chalcolithic.
What was life like then? Agriculture had begun. Animals had been domesticated and were being exploited for their meat, with dairying only arising much later.
Populations were growing and changing. The Chalcolithic was a time of mass migrations, the authors write, including to what is now Israel, where archaeologists observe a sea change in pottery in that era.
Analyses of ancient DNA also reveal population changes. It seems that this was when the first centralized proto-states began to emerge, and occasional spats developed into large-scale war, bigger than in the Sudan and Turkana in prehistory. Now, it wasn’t groups armed with arrows and spears and stones, but massive armies on the march.
Moreover, the authors say that they do not detect an “urban effect” – the Chalcolithic surge wasn’t necessarily confined to the proto-cities.
Lethal aggression then declined sharply in the Early Bronze Age, and even more so in the Middle Bronze Age, from 5,000 to 3,500 years ago. Somehow, internal violence within Bronze Age Mesopotamian societies diminished, though it seems the kings partly redirected hawkishness towards external enemies.
This was concluded based on lower levels of injury in Mesopotamia and by the match between the concentration of traumatic injuries and the royal inscriptions documenting Mesopotamian campaigns along the eastern borders. Maybe hordes of testosterone-riddled young men were sent to fight other people. The authors don’t say that, but it’s a thought.
All fall down
The transition from the Late Bronze Age to the Iron Age brought another spike in bloodshed. That period was marked by upheavals, too. The aforementioned mega-drought led to resource stress and mass population displacements.
Established powers collapsed. The Egyptians had to retreat back to Egypt. Empires folded throughout the Levant and Iran. This period was followed by the rise of the regional superpowers of antiquity, such as the Assyrian Empire, which expanded not by handing out flowers but by military campaigns and mass deportations, the authors sum up. They draw a possible parallel to climatic havoc in Inca-period highland Peru, spurring competition over resources and an escalation in lethal conflict.
The authors also suspect that trade played a hand in the rise, fall, re-rise, etc., of lethal violence. Trade expansion peaked between the late Early Bronze Age and the early Middle Bronze Age, a relatively quiescent period, violence-wise. Similar patterns are reported from Medieval Europe and the Americas.
So, is it case closed? No, but the authors explain they “can confirm for this specific case of the Ancient Middle East that the violence decline took place at a time when early states achieved substantial capacities to reduce conflicts in their societies and then increased again” between the Late Bronze Age and the Iron Age (1,500–400 B.C.E.), as empires writhed and the entire region was in upheaval. At this stage, the requisite conclusion seems to be that we are neither hawks nor doves. When times get rough, we protect our own – but our aggression can be kept in check by civilization.

TITLE: Israeli Army Prepares for Ground Invasion in Gaza Amid Rocket Barrages From Gaza, Lebanon
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-14T08:35:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-14/ty-article-live/idf-kills-hamas-head-of-aerial-forces-strikes-dozens-of-gaza-targets-overnight/0000018b-2c64-da5e-abef-ad656b090000

Updates
IDF: We assassinated the Hamas commander who was responsible for the raid on Kibbutz Nirim and Nir Oz
The IDF and the Shin Bet announced that they had assassinated Bilal al-Kadra, the commander of the Noh'ba force (Hamas' special forces) in the South Khan Yunis battalion, who was responsible for the raid on the Nirim and Nir Oz kibbutzim on Saturday.
According to the announcement, other Hamas and Islamic Jihad operatives were killed in attacks overnight in Zeitoon, Khan Yunis and Jabaliya. It was also reported that the IDF attacked headquarters and military compounds, dozens of launchers, anti-tank posts and observation posts belonging to Hamas.
New poll shows 65 percent of Americans believe U.S. should publicly support Israel in its war
65 percent of Americans believe the U.S. should publicly support Israel in its war with Hamas, according to a new NPR/PBS NewsHour/Marist poll.
23 percent of Americans believe the U.S. should say or do nothing, while only 8 percent believe it should publicly criticize Israel.
69 percent of Democrats back Israel, compared to 77 percent of Republicans and 54 independents.
Only 48 percent of Gen Z/millenials believe the U.S. should back Israel —compared to 63 percent of Gen X, 83 percent of Baby boomers and 86 percent of the Silent/Greatest generation.
51 percent of nonwhites said the U.S. should take such a public stance supporting Israel, while 72 percent of whites thought it should.
The survey of 1,313 adults was conducted Wednesday and has a margin of error of +/- 3.8 percentage points, meaning results could be about 4 points lower or higher. Respondents were reached by telephone using live interviewers, by text or online.
U.S. deploying second carrier strike group near Israel as Gaza ground invasion looms
The U.S. will deploy a second aircraft carrier strike group near Israel, further bolstering its military presence in the Mediterranean amid concerns of an escalating conflict with Iran and Hezbollah.
U.S. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin said that "The increases to U.S. force posture signal the United States' ironclad commitment to Israel’s security and our resolve to deter any state or non-state actor seeking to escalate this war."
U.S. Secretary of State Blinken speaks with Chinese Foreign Minister
U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken spoke with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, where he stressed U.S. support for Israel alongside demanding Hamas cease its actions and release all hostages.
"The Secretary also discussed the importance of maintaining stability in the region and discouraging other parties from entering the conflict," the State Department noted – a particularly relevant point considering China's warm relationship with Iran.
U.S. President Joe Biden speaks at 2023 Human Rights Campaign Dinner
Speaking at the event, Biden's remarks included reference to the war in Israel and Gaza.
Biden said that "We saw hate manifested another way in the worst massacre of Jewish people since the Holocaust," and also made note of "the humanitarian crisis in Gaza – innocent Palestinian families, the vast majority have nothing to do Hamas and being used as human shields."
"We have to reject hate in every form," Biden said, "because history has taught us again and again. Antisemitism, Islamophobia, homophobia, transphobia. They're all connected. Hate toward one group left unanswered opens the door for more hate for more groups."
Dozens of people gather to protest outside the home of journalist Israel Frey
Dozens of people are gathering outside the home of journalist Israel Frey in Bnei Brak, and are inciting against him.
"Just like you wouldn't let a secular person live in your building," one of them read in a proclamation, "don't let a murderer live in your building." In addition, chants of "traitor" were called and the sounds of explosions were heard.
Frey reported that some were trying to enter his residential building, but the police at the scene claim that no such attempt is known.
Since the beginning of the war, Frey, a leftist and ultra-Orthodox journalist, has been targeted by the right-wing for his various statements against Israeli policies. In particular, Frey was criticized for a video in which he can be heard reciting Kaddish in memory of the victims of the war, including innocent Gaza residents who were killed in recent IDF strikes.
IDF attacks tunnel in the Gaza Strip
The IDF spokesman announced that Hamas operatives were seen coming out of a tunnel in Gaza. The tunnel was attacked by an IDF aircraft, killing the operatives.
It was also reported that the IDF attacked other locations across the Gaza Strip, mainly in the neighborhoods of Jabaliya, Zeytun, Al-Furqan and Beit Hanoun.
Iran's Foreign Minister meets with Hamas' Political Bureau Chief
Iran's Foreign Minister, Hossein Amir Abdollahian, met with the head of Hamas' political bureau, Ismail Haniyeh, in Qatar.
Earlier today, the Iranian Foreign Minister met in Beirut with the Secretary General of Islamic Jihad, Ziad Anchala, and with the Deputy Head of the Political Bureau of Hamas, Salah al-Aruri.

TITLE: Hamas planned to kill and abduct civilians, documents retrieved from the deadly assault reveal
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-14T13:34:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-14/ty-article/hamas-planned-to-kill-and-abduct-civilians-documents-from-the-deadly-assault-reveal/0000018b-2d74-dff1-a5eb-fffde4b70000

Hamas terrorists who attacked Israel's Gaza border communities last Saturday were found with detailed maps and documentation, indicating their intention to take over educational institutions and abduct citizens, including children.
On Friday, the New York Times and NBC News released two extensive articles detailing how the attack was meticulously planned and was originally aimed to harm civilians, including children. The terrorist group attempted to claim that kidnapping people was not an official objective of the attack.
The documents were discovered in the custody of Hamas militants who took part in the deadly assault, according to American media reports. One of the documents explicitly stated that the attack was meant "to capture soldiers and civilians to be used as bargaining chips."
According to the New York Times, one of the documents was dated October 2022, demonstrating the extensive planning that went into the assault. It also featured videos released by Hamas from the raid, showing at least one militant carrying a map of one of the kibbutzim.
BREAKING: Hamas intentionally targeted elementary schools in Israel, instructed terrorists to seize hostages, move them into Gaza, and to "kill as many people as possible," maps and documents recovered from the bodies of attackers show. nbcnews.com/news/investiga…
NBC reported that one source within the IDF and another within the Israeli government verified that Israel seized dozens of documents labeled "top secret" in Arabic.
According to the report, one of the documents revealed the attack strategy in the kibbutz of Sa'ad, where the militants failed to penetrate the community and were repelled by the community security force.
The plan involved two Hamas units. One was tasked with taking control of the new Da'at school in the kibbutz, and the other was responsible for searching the old school and the Bnei Akiva youth facility to take hostages.
According to another document published by NBC, the units were told to "kill as many as possible." Additional seized documents show Hamas had intelligence on every community near the Gaza border and devised plans for each of them, including the targeting of women and children, according to Israeli sources who spoke with NBC.
"The level of specificity would cause anyone in the intelligence field's jaw to drop," the army official quoted in the stated article.
A senior IDF officer who spoke with The New York Times stated that the militants who infiltrated the army bases and were positioned near the border acted ruthlessly and even fired at soldiers in their living quarters. The officer went on to say that in other cases, militants were aware of the location of communication equipment and servers and rushed to destroy them. This made it difficult for the troops on the ground to understand the full picture of the situation and respond quickly to the attack.
The report also noted that Hamas divided the groups involved in the extensive incursion into smaller forces and assigned members duties such as drivers, navigators, and demolition experts. Additionally, the organization provided artillery cover in the form of mortar fire for the militants who infiltrated the kibbutzim and military posts.
Furthermore, the documents indicate that Hamas provided its assessment units with information about the number of soldiers at each post, how many vehicles were at their disposal, and how long it would take them to reach each kibbutz.
Some of the units involved in the assault were instructed to ambush key junctions along the border area to prevent the IDF from sending reinforcements, as reported by four official sources who spoke with The New York Times, including military officers.

TITLE: U.S. Embassy organizes emergency evacuation by ship for Americans wanting to leave Israel
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-15T12:10:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-15/ty-article/u-s-embassy-organizes-emergency-ship-for-americans-wanting-to-leave-israel/0000018b-3285-dff1-a5eb-fefd8f920000

A ship for American citizens wishing to leave Israel will be departing from Haifa on Monday morning, the U.S. Embassy in Israel announced Sunday.
The Cyprus-bound boat is designated for “U.S. nationals and their immediate family members with a valid travel document,” the announcement said.
On Friday, the White House and State Department announced the start of chartered flights for American citizens departing Israel to Athens and Frankfurt in order to “facilitate the safe departure of thousands of U.S. citizens.”
White House National Security Council spokesman John Kirby told reporters on the same day that the U.S. government was investigating ways to accommodate demand for travel out of Israel, “including exploring whether it’s possible to help Americans leave by land and by sea” to increase capacity.
Monday’s boat trip from Haifa is not free: Those who board the ship, like those who are taking advantage of the chartered flights, will be required to sign an agreement to repay the U.S. government for the cost of the trip.
Those on board will be responsible for arranging their own accommodations and onward travel from Cyprus, adding that if travelers “are unable to secure onward travel from Cyprus, chartered flights are also being arranged.”
Travel to the ship’s departure site in Haifa “is conducted at your own risk, and plans may change depending on the security situation. The U.S. government is unable to guarantee your safety,” the announcement stated.
The embassy announcement said the sea journey to Limassol would take approximately 10 to 12 hours, that each traveler would be permitted to bring a 50-pound (22.5-kilogram) suitcase and carry-on bag, and that pets would not be permitted to board. Food and Wi-Fi will be provided on the ship, the announcement said, and upon arrival in Limassol, buses will transport travelers to the country’s international airports in Larnaca and Paphos.
On Saturday, an embassy announcement said the U.S. government was also “working on potential options for departure from Gaza for U.S. citizens” – with the caveat that the “military conflict between Israel and Hamas is ongoing, making identifying departure options for U.S. citizens” in the Strip “complex.”

TITLE: Israeli army chief says goal to enter Gaza and cripple Hamas; Herzog reveals Hamas 'torture manual'
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-15T13:45:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-15/ty-article-live/israeli-army-prepares-for-ground-invasion-in-gaza-kills-hamas-commander-who-led-massacres/0000018b-311e-dff1-a5eb-ffff91120000

Updates
Biden considering trip to Israel in the coming days, but travel isn’t final
President Joe Biden is considering a trip to Israel in the coming days but no travel has been finalized, a senior administration official said Sunday. It would be a powerful symbol of sympathy and support following the brutal attack by Hamas.
A trip would be a chance for Biden to personally affirm to the Israeli people the U.S. is standing firm behind them. But it would come amid growing fears that a looming Israeli move into Gaza could spark a wider war with devastating humanitarian consequences.
And Biden’s presence could be seen as a provocative move by Hamas’ chief sponsor, Iran, or potentially viewed as tone-deaf by Arab nations as civilian casualties mount in Gaza. Secretary of State Antony Blinken has already been traveling around the Mideast this past week trying to prevent the war with Hamas from igniting a broader regional conflict.
The official could not publicly discuss internal deliberations about the potential presidential travel and spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity.
U.S. offered Hamas humanitarian aid in exchange for release of civilian hostages, Lebanese newspaper reports
The Lebanese Al-Akhbar newspaper reported that the U.S. submitted a compromise proposal to Hamas for the release of kidnapped civilians in Gaza in exchange for humanitarian aid to the Strip.
According to the report, which was signed by the editor of the newspaper Abraham Al-Nim, who is close to senior Hamas officials and the Hezbollah leadership, Hamas set several conditions, and demanded to find out which of the abductees were foreign citizens and which of them served in the IDF.
Rafah border crossing between Gaza and Egypt set to open on Monday morning, saying U.S. Embassy in Israel
Citing media reports, the U.S. Embassy in Israel said the Rafah border crossing will open at 9 AM local time on October 16.
"We anticipate that the situation at the Rafah crossing will remain fluid and unpredictable and it is unclear whether, or for how long, travelers will be permitted to transit the crossing," the embassy said.
"If you assess it to be safe, you may wish to move closer to the Rafah border crossing – there may be very little notice if the crossing opens and it may only open for a limited time," the embassy added.
Israel has no intention to reoccupy Gaza, says Israel's UN ambassador
Israel's Ambassador to the UN Gilad Erdan, in response to Biden's interview, said it has no intention to reoccupy Gaza following its ground invasion in response to the Hamas attack.
"We have no interest to occupy Gaza or to stay in Gaza, but since we are fighting for our survival, and the only way – as the President himself defined – is to obliterate Hamas, we will have to do whatever is needed to obliterate their capabilities," he told CNN's Kaitlan Collins.
Erdan avoided answering what he imagines Gaza's power structure to resemble following Hamas' dismantlement, saying "we would like to be coordinated with our American allies. But for now, the only focus should be how to release the hostages, how to secure our future by obliterating Hamas' capabilities."
U.S. Senate Majority Leader to push Israel aid package
Israeli officials told visiting U.S. senators that they are requesting precision-guided munitions, Iron Dome missile defense system replenishments, 155-millimeter mortar shells, small-diameter bombs and JDAM kits that convert unguided bombs into precision munitions.
Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer detailed the requested aid, adding intelligence and diplomatic assistance to the list.
Schumer is expected to make the aid package a priority, despite the fact the House has yet to name a new speaker.
"We're not waiting for the House. We believe that if the Senate acts in a strong bipartisan way it may indeed improve the chances that the House, even with its current dysfunction, will act," he said.
U.S. officials said earlier this weekend that they will be holding intensive talks with Congress about the supplementary aid package, which will likely be paired with some combination of assistance for Ukraine, Taiwan and border security.
Efforts to normalize relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia are not dead, says Biden
In unaired footage posted online, Biden denied that efforts to normalize relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia were dead following the attack.
"The Saudis, and the Emiratis and other Arab nations understand that their security and stability is enhanced if there's normalization of relations with Israel," Biden said.
"It's just going to take time to get done, he said, "but the direction, moving into the normalization makes sense for the Arab nations as well as Israel."
Biden as Israel's ground invasion looms: It would be a mistake to reoccupy Gaza
U.S. President Joe Biden said he believes it would be a mistake for Israel to re-occupy Gaza, in his first interview since the Hamas attack on Israel and as Israel's ground invasion looms.
Speaking to CBS' 60 Minutes – America's most-watched news program – Biden reiterated that the U.S. will do everything in its power to free hostages held captive in Gaza, saying "we're working like hell on it."
Violent anti-Israel graffiti appears in San Francisco following a pro-Palestine rally
Windows in San Francisco were defaced with violent anti-Israel graffiti following a pro-Palestinian rally.
Among the hateful language scrawled include "death to Zionism," "kill a settler" and "death 2 Israel."
We are deeply disturbed by graffiti along Market Street reading after yesterday's pro-Palestinian rally in San Francisco. We have been in touch with city leaders and @SFPD to investigate this crime.

TITLE: Confirming the worst Hamas atrocities: Inside Israel's center for the identification of the dead
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-15T15:14:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-15/ty-article-magazine/confirming-the-worst-hamas-atrocities-where-israel-identifies-the-dead/0000018b-3313-dff1-a5eb-ffffee6f0000

The first thing that hits you upon entering the center for identification of the dead next to Ramle is the unbearable stench of death. No mask can protect you from it. The Shura military base – which under normal circumstances is the main camp of the Israeli army’s Rabbinate – has become an end point. It is a horrific drainage basin into which the terrible river of the dead empties, until the deceased are sent to their final rest.
On Friday, almost a week after the war broke out, members of the Israeli and international media were allowed onto the base to show the world some of the horrors carried out by Hamas in the communities near Gaza. The Israel Defense Forces spokesperson aims to reveal what the murderers did, but at the same time urged that we avoid detail that would spill into death porn.
According to the people involved in handling the bodies, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s description of beheaded babies is accurate.
The sights are hard to grasp. The feelings at this place, to which more and more bodies are being brought, are impossible to put into words. The work of identifying the dead is methodical, like on an assembly line.
There is a long line of 13 containers at the site. Each contains 44 bodies and body parts whose identification has been completed.
The door to one of the containers is opened to us, to take photographs. We receive explanations. The workers here have been here around the clock since October 7. Many are volunteers with the ultra-Orthodox Zaka organization (which retrieves bodies and body parts after terror attacks). Some belong to Unit 360, a relatively new national organization that also engages in identifying the victims. Others are civilian employees with the army, while there are others too – people accustomed to dealing with the dead on a daily basis, identifying the victims of disaster and preserving their dignity.
At the edge of the compound is a refrigerated truck containing bodies that have been identified and released for burial. It is being loaded. The process is a lengthy one. Hundreds of families already have dead to bury and others have yet to receive verified information about their loved ones. Never before has Israel set up a project to engage in handling and identifying victims within a day.
The workers wear gloves, masks and protective clothing. They look exhausted, from every perspective. The mob of journalists seems to have burst into their world. None readily stepped up to talk with us and tell us what they had seen.
“I have been here since Sunday,” says Zaka volunteer Haim Oter. “The ones here” – in that container – “are only the ones who have been identified. I have been unloading and loading the bodies all week.”
How is he coping? “It’s not new to me,” Oter responds. “I routinely volunteer with the Chevra kadisha [burial society] in washing bodies.”
Benny Schechter, also volunteering for Zaka, arrived the day before from the Golan Heights. “Some of the bodies are in a very bad state,” he says. “They weren’t just shot dead. Some are very hard to identify because they were burned. In some cases, you find the body and head separately. There were body parts found in the trees. It’s a cruelty that is very hard to describe. I told the family I would stay here all of Shabbat to continue working.”
Shlomit Landes, head of the Israel Police’s investigations unit, is presently running this compound. Hundreds of police officers are there too, working around the clock, she says. “Some of them never dealt with dead bodies before,” she says. “Many of them can’t take it.”
The whole world needs to understand that the descriptions voiced time again and again by Israel’s leaders aren’t exaggerated, Lt. Col. Richard Hecht, international spokesman for the Israel Defense Forces, tells the foreign reporters. This is the same as ISIS.
“We spent three days with the [international media], so they understand the scope of the massacre that happened here – because from [Sunday] they will start to accuse us of being war criminals,” he says. “The IDF only aims at Hamas, not the civilian population. We do not attack children. Hamas uses them as human shields. Every soldier in the IDF should visit this place too, to understand what’s going on here, and what happened.”

TITLE: Sara Netanyahu's bureau chief under fire for 'traitors' social media posts
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-15T16:50:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-15/ty-article/sara-netanyahus-bureau-chief-under-fire-for-traitors-social-media-posts/0000018b-3323-d450-a3af-7b3f0fb60000

Israel’s Civil Service Commission has demanded the suspension of Sara Netanyahu’s bureau chief and close advisor Tzipi Navon, following a series of social media posts in which she lashed out at various political opponents of the Prime Minister and his wife, calling them “traitors,” “traitorous Jews,” “scum,” and other derogatory terms.

TITLE: Musk’s X and Hamas’ digital offensive: Gaza is a perfect storm of disinformation
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-15T17:34:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/security-aviation/2023-10-15/ty-article/musks-x-and-hamas-digital-offensive-gaza-is-a-perfect-storm-of-disinformation/0000018b-3331-d450-a3af-7b3d6a050000

As Hamas terrorists entered Israel to begin the ruthless slaughter of innocent Israelis, the terror group also began a digital onslaught online, with numerous fake accounts linked to the group pushing out propaganda videos and glorifying posts. The Israel-Hamas war is a perfect storm of disinformation, experts say, unprecedented in scale. This, they explain, is thanks to a convergence of factors, including influence campaigns by Iran and Hamas, buoyed by an ecosystem of right-wing conspiracy theories, and Elon Musk’s changes to X (formerly Twitter).
Israelis will remember this war as one of the most devastating events in the country's history. The incompetence that led to the horrific massacres in the Gaza border communities was exacerbated by a lack of response to the digital offensive launched by the terror group and its supporters. This included disinformation, misinformation and massive amounts of propaganda that helped create chaos on the Israeli home front. For example, during the first hours of the attacks and in recent days again, fake accounts linked to Iran claimed they useful launched a cyber attack against Israel.
Hackers may have failed to hurt Israeli civilian infrastructure, it remains unknown – but a known Iranian influence network managed to spread the rumor to sow panic. For the past two days, this unverified messages about an imagined cyber-attack reached every corner of Israel and beyond.
"This is a well-known Iranian network that operates over 1,000 accounts and, until recently, interfered mainly with internal Israeli matters," says Achiya Schatz, CEO of Fake Reporter, which uncovered the activities.
A fake BBC video claiming a Bellingcat investigation shows Ukraine smuggled weapons to Hamas is being pushed by Russian social media users. It's unclear if this is a Russian government disinformation campaign or a grassroots effort, but it's 100% fake t.me/sheyhtamir1974…
Show more
"This is a sophisticated network that has thus far promoted political content designed to divide the Israeli public. Upon the war's outbreak, it started promoting content such as a [false] cyber-attack, and later fake videos related to [Israeli far-right nationalist group] La Familia."
Many analysts suspect Russia-aligned groups have also joined the fake news game. They note as one example a video spread on a Telegram page previously linked to the Doppelganger campaign, a worldwide Russian influence campaign exposed by Haaretz and other outlets earlier this year.
In another case, a video was released claiming Ukraine was helping Hamas; this week a fake document was released alleged to be an official document showing the U.S. would provide Israel with $8 billion in aid.
Nearly half a million accounts on Facebook, Instagram, X, and TikTok posted about the war during the first 48 hours, according to data from Cyabra, which tracks false information online - and a quarter were fake accounts. Content from them reached hundreds of thousands of people in Israel and abroad, says Dan Brahmy, the company's CEO. Alongside the false information, the accounts also posted Hamas propaganda about the attacks, sharing snuff videos and photos of the organization's drones dropping grenades on Israeli tanks.
Thread: Online misinformation is rampant following the escalation of violence between Israel and Hamas today. This video of a tower block in Gaza being hit by a missile is from May 2021, not today. It was captured live during a BBC Arabic broadcast at the time.
Show more
Hamas’ disinformation efforts, and those influence operations organized by foreign states, have received an unexpected boost from recent changes at X. Under Elon Musk, X has taken a series of steps that have undone years of anti-disinformation efforts, taking apart different mechanisms put in place to quell false information on the popular social network. By charging money for verified account status (the “blue check”), the platform has made it extremely simple for anonymous entities to impersonate well-trusted accounts, and virtually eliminated mechanisms to protect against malicious activity.
Musk recently terminated his contract with the Israeli company ActiveFence, which provided X with content monitoring services, further damaging the platform's ability to filter out fake and offensive content. ActiveFence is now also focusing on monitoring false information about the Gaza war.
"There is no more monitoring of offensive content, which explains the amount of snuff videos that accounts associated with Hamas and Iran have published unhindered – and there is no more automatic monitoring of coordinated inauthentic activity, i.e., locating and removing bot networks or automated avatars that work together in an organized manner," says a senior researcher from Intercept 9500, a business intelligence firm that detects foreign malicious activity online.
Several researchers told Haaretz that X’s policy changes opened the door for fake accounts that would have once been removed within hours remaining on the air for two or three days.
This video certainly doesn't show Israeli fighter jets about to "rain down hellfire" on Gaza. It's from the video game Arma 3. It was posted to TikTok last night racking up 1.7 million views, and has now been shared by Britian First leader Paul Golding.
Show more
That's not Cristiano Ronaldo holding the Palestinian flag. That's Moroccan footballer Jawad El Yamiq, and the video is from the 2022 World Cup. This account poses as a BBC journalist using a picture of a Pakistani sports presenter to share misinformation for engagement.
Volunteer civilians, cyber firms, and civil society organizations are partially filling the space left by the state and X. But It’s not only organized influence operations that are benefitting from this – it has also led to misinformation shared in good faith by innocent people go viral. Pictures of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad’s chemical weapons slaughter of civilians, for example, were presented as if they were from the aftermath of an Israeli attack on Gaza. Such examples abound from both sides of the war.
“The extent of misinformation on Twitter in this war is the greatest I have seen in my life," says Shayan Sardarizadeh, a BBC journalist specializing in disinformation, conspiracy theory, and data validation. Over the past week, he has been closely following false information circulating online and deftly refuting it.
But despite his and the best efforts by the different volunteer groups, they, too, can't stanch the flow. "In the first few hours on Saturday, there was a terrible information vacuum – the government wasn't talking. This vacuum allowed elements from abroad, but unfortunately also from within Israel, to operate," says Schatz.
Thread: Online misinformation about the Israel-Hamas conflict - Day 5 This video, viewed nearly 300,000 times, falsely claims to show Israel drop white phospherus bombs on Gaza. The video is from March, and shows Russia using incendiary munitions in Vuhledar, Ukraine.
Show more
Together with the Israel Internet Association, FakeReporter established an “anti-fake news war room” for center for mapping and debunking disinformation. They dubbed it the Fakes Command Center. It works around the clock to find false information on a range of platforms, including semi-closed networks like WhatsApp and Telegram.
FakeReporter researchers found that fake accounts operating in Hebrew had taken over the hashtags "Re'im massacre" and "Re'im party," which reached Twitter's trending topics and Facebook's recommended list. The accounts promoted false propaganda such as innumerable videos depicting Hamas attacks as Israeli aggression, and old videos re-used for new deceptions.
Accounts linked to Hamas and Iran boosted posts falsely alleging that Israeli forces were attacking the Al-Aqsa Mosque, attempting to justify Hamas' attacks. Later, videos were released in which Hamas members depicted treating hostages humanely in a bid to cover up their atrocities. Other accounts linked to the same networks distributed snuff videos.
Conspiratorial
The unprecedented terrorist attack of October 7 left one resounding question: how could this happen? One of the popular answers is a conspiracy theory blaming the IDF, the Shin Bet, and the rest of the security leadership that warned of defense consequences of the government’s judicial overhaul.
According to this conspiracy theory, spread by Iranian accounts but also by supporters of the current government, Israel’s military elite betrayed the people of Israel and purposefully allowed Hamas’ attacks to take place. The narrative is reminiscent of the stab-in-the-back myth that preceded the rise of the Nazis in Germany.
The researchers can't say for sure where the betrayal narrative began. According to an Intercept 9500 review, it has been echoed by fake accounts that have long been known to be linked to Iran.

TITLE: Biden to visit Israel on Wednesday; Hamas releases first video of French-Israeli hostage
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-16T08:22:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-16/ty-article-live/israel-prepares-for-ground-invasion-biden-big-mistake-to-reoccupy-gaza/0000018b-364f-dc99-a1db-3fcf1ae10000

Updates
IDF chief to soldiers: We are responsible for the hard hit Israel took
A meaningful letter from the IDF Chief of the General Staff, LTG Herzi Halevi, to fellow soldiers, commanders and reservists:
IDF Chief of Staff Herzl Halevi sent a letter to Israeli soldiers on Tuesday, 10 days after the massive Hamas attack that left at least 1,300 Israelis dead and dozens in captivity in the Gaza Strip.
“We suffered a hard hit and we are responsible – but now the initiative is in our hands.”
Halevi added that “the war will difficult and long and the IDF will prevail.”
Senior U.S. general makes unannounced visit to Israel as war with Hamas deepens
The top U.S. general overseeing American forces in the Middle East made an unannounced trip to Israel on Tuesday, saying he hoped to ensure its military has what it needs as it fights a deepening war against Palestinian militant group Hamas.
The trip by Army General Michael "Erik" Kurilla, head of U.S. Central Command, is the latest by a senior U.S. official to Israel ahead of an expected ground assault by Israel's military in Gaza. It comes a day before a planned visit by U.S. President Joe Biden to the country.
The U.S. military is increasing its firepower in the region, aiming to prevent Iran and other Iran-backed groups from getting involved in the conflict as international fears of a wider, regional war grow.
The Pentagon is also rushing weaponry, including air defenses and munitions, to Israel.
"I'm here to ensure Israel has what it needs to defend itself, particularly focused on avoiding other parties expanding the conflict," Kurilla told Reuters, which is traveling with him, in brief remarks before landing.
A U.S. official told Reuters Kurilla was scheduled to hold high-level meetings with Israel's military leadership, ensuring a clear understanding of the close U.S. ally's defense requirements.
Kurilla was also expected to outline U.S. military support aimed at avoiding an expansion of the Israel-Hamas conflict.
U.S. confirms: Biden visit finalized after Israel committed to Gaza aid package
A U.S. official confirmed a Washington Post report that Blinken waited to announce U.S. President Joe Biden's visit to Israel on Wednesday until receiving commitments from Netanyahu concerning a Gaza humanitarian aid package and the creation of civilian safe-zones at the conclusion of the secretary's eight-hour meeting with Israel's war cabinet.
New York Times: Biden visit could delay Israeli ground operation in Gaza
The New York Times reported Tuesday that U.S. President Joe Biden’s visit to Israel on Wednesday will delay Israel’s planned ground operation in the Gaza Strip for at least 24 hours.
The IDF’s spokesperson for the foreign press, Jonathan Conricus, responded to questions about the timing of an Israeli ground operation by saying, “We’ll have to wait and see.”
Conricus added that Israel’s announcement telling Gazans to leave their homes was a significant strategic risk from an Israeli perspective, but said it was intended to safeguard the lives of civilians in the Strip. “We have no desire whatsoever to kill or hurt noncombatants,” he said.
The New York Times also reported that Israel has requested emergency aid from the U.S. to the tune of $10 billion.
New York Governor on way to Israel as part of solidarity mission
New York Governor Kathy Hochul is on her way to Israel as part of a solidarity mission. In a post on X, the social media platform formerly known as Twitter, she wrote that she would be meeting with diplomatic leaders and communities devastated by the “horrific Hamas attacks.”
“New York will always stand with Israel,” she wrote.
Hochul was one of the keynote speakers at a large rally in solidarity with Israel held last week outside the United Nations. Saying she was “proud to govern the state with the largest Jewish population outside Israel,” Hochul tried to reassure those in the crowd who might be feeling vulnerable because of the atrocities committed against Jews in Israel. “We will make sure we stand together to protect every single one of you,” she promised
U.S. President Joe Biden will visit Israel on Wednesday
WASHINGTON - U.S. President Joe Biden will visit Israel on Wednesday, U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken announced Tuesday after a nearly eight-hour long meeting with Israeli officials in Tel Aviv.
Blinken told reporters that the president would arrive to show unshakable support to Israel and speak first-hand with Israeli leaders about the hostages held captive in Gaza, as well as the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

TITLE: Deadly Hamas rampage constitutes 'international crime of genocide,' hundreds of legal experts say
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-16T14:04:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-16/ty-article/hamas-deadly-rampage-constitutes-crime-of-genocide-hundreds-of-legal-experts-say/0000018b-37d1-d450-a3af-7fddda070000

Hamas' October 7 massacre of over 1,300 Israelis and foreign citizens constituted the “crime of genocide,” hundreds of international jurists and academics, including the former Justice Minister of Canada, declared Monday.
In an open letter, some 240 legal experts, including experts from Harvard and Columbia Law Schools, King's College London and the Hebrew University in Jerusalem, asserted that last weekend’s attack constituted a “gross violation of international law, and, in particular, of international criminal law.”
According to Israeli news site Ynet, the letter was the initiative of former acting State Prosecutor Dan Eldad and ex-Deputy Attorney General Raz Nizri.
“As these widespread, horrendous acts appear to have been carried out with an ‘intent to destroy, in whole or in part’ a national group – Israelis – a goal explicitly declared by Hamas, they most probably constitute an international crime of genocide, proscribed by the Genocide Convention and the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court,” the letter stated, adding that Hamas had kidnapped over 150 people, most of whom are civilians.
“Among those abducted there are women, children, infants, elderly people in need of medical care and people with disabilities. According to media reports, some kidnapped persons were murdered following their abduction. Videos, released mostly by Hamas, posted on social media, document acts of torture, sexual violence, violence towards children and molestation of bodies,” the jurists stated, noting that “international law prohibits the taking of hostages,” which is “defined as a war crime.”
On Monday morning, the IDF Spokesperson’s office confirmed that 199 Israelis have been kidnapped and are being held hostage in the Gaza Strip.
“The laws pertaining to the holding of prisoners of war do not apply to terrorist organizations,” the experts asserted, stating that, as such, “holding both civilian and soldier hostages constitutes a war crime” and that they must be released immediately.
Additionally, they continued, “members of Hamas deliberately targeted their attacks against large numbers of civilians, committing murder, torture, rape, mutilation and molestation of bodies. Each of these acts constitutes a war crime, for which perpetrators must bear full accountability.”
Among the signatories of the letter were Adv. Vadim Shub, public defender at the Jerusalem District Court, Adv. Yuval Kaplinsky, Former Director of the Department of International Affairs, Israel’s State Attorney’s Office, former New Israel Fund president Naomi Chazan, and former Canadian Justice Minister Irwin Cotler.
The Raoul Wallenberg Centre for Human Rights, which Cotler chairs, recently made headlines with a report on the Russian invasion of Ukraine claiming that Moscow was carrying out a genocide against the Ukrainian people.
The letter was also signed by Cornell University’s Prof. Menachem Rosensaft, an expert on the laws of genocide and, until recently, executive vice president of the World Jewish Congress.
In article published last Thursday in Newsweek, Rosensaft asserted that “Hamas has never wavered from its determination to perpetrate the genocide of Jews living in Israel,” citing its charter’s declaration that “Israel will exist and will continue to exist until Islam will obliterate it.”
He also cited Hamas co-founder Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi’s pledge that “we will not leave one Jew in Palestine,” arguing that such rhetoric proved that “Hamas is determined not just to obliterate the State of Israel but to ravage and kill the Jews living there as it did on Oct. 7.”
Mondays’ letter comes only days after the heads of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem sent a strongly worded letter to their counterparts at Harvard University and Stanford University, criticizing their responses to declarations of solidarity with Hamas terrorists at their elite institutions.
Jewish students at universities across the United States have said that they are shocked and stunned by the responses of campus groups affiliated with the progressive and radical left to the brutal attacks on Israeli civilians by Hamas.
In one case, the president of the NYU Student Bar Association publicly declared that she wanted to “express, first and foremost, my unwavering and absolute solidarity with Palestinians in their resistance against oppression toward liberation and self-determination,” a statement which was later repudiated by NYU Dean Troy McKenzie.
Judy Maltz contributed to this report.

TITLE: Hamas Abducted Her Daughters: 'I'm Sorry, but I Don’t Believe God Exists'
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-16T14:41:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-16/ty-article-magazine/i-dont-believe-god-exists-if-he-does-why-are-my-daughters-in-gaza/0000018b-3810-df29-a5ab-fe7f29520000

A year and a half ago, a few weeks after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, I traveled to Poland with photographer Michal Halbin and producer Yasmin Harel to record in words and photos the stories of Ukrainian women who had fled their country with their children and found refuge with Polish host families.
Among the heart-wrenching stories of women and children who had managed to escape ruined houses and cities through peril, we discovered a great deal of kindness and boundless human generosity.
Early last week, two days after this still-nameless, terrible war began and as the enormity of the horrors perpetrated on towns near the Gaza border was just starting to emerge, the terror of that far-off war in Europe arrived at Israel’s doorstep. We were struggling with feelings of helplessness, sympathy for the victims and their families, and paralyzing anxiety over the fate of the hostages. We felt the only way to handle it was to once more portray the stories and the faces and use them to stitch our sense of reality back together again.
Brig. Gen. (res.) Gal Hirsch, tasked with overseeing the return of hostages and the missing, announced on Monday that official notifications had been sent to the families of 199 Israelis held in Gaza. We have collected the stories and recollections of some of their families, who are profoundly anxious as they wait to learn the fates of their loved ones.
Maayan Zin, mother of Dafna (15) and Ella (8)
Maayan Zin isn’t praying. “I'm sorry, but I don’t believe God exists,” she says. “If he does, why are my daughters in Gaza? Why all this murder along the Gaza border? Why did they bring families there to fill kibbutzim, with innocent children now going through what they are?”
Dafna and Ella, Maayan’s daughters, were kidnapped to Gaza from the home of their father, Noam Elkayam. Also kidnapped with them were Noam and his partner, Dikla, along with Tomer, Dikla’s 17-year-old son from a previous marriage.
Noam and Maayan divorced nine years ago while she was pregnant with Ella. The family previously lived in Arad. Both Dafna and Ella were born after Maayan received lengthy, difficult fertility treatments. After the divorce, Noam moved to Nahal Oz on the Gaza border, and Maayan moved to Be’er Sheva to find work. The divorce left her with nothing.
“I didn’t work before the divorce. I was busy with the fertility treatments and then with raising Dafna. That was my entire life. My entire life revolved around the attempts to get Dafna before she arrived. I started looking for work after the divorce.
I moved to Be’er Sheva and started working as a rehab counsellor for people dealing with mental illness,” she continues. I did that for a while until Ella was born. The work helped me a lot emotionally, more than the money did. I worked as both a counsellor and a maid. On days the girls were with Noam, I worked from morning to night with people in rehab and cleaning houses.
“But it wasn’t enough, since Ella was a baby who needed to be taken to and from day care. That left me with maybe six hours a day for working, other than days they were with Noam,” she says.
Two years after the divorce, Maayan could no longer meet the expenses of raising two daughters. She had to ask Noam to let Dafna move in with him and his new partner in Nahal Oz. “Otherwise, they would never have been able to go there, even on visits,” she says. “I think it’s irresponsible to live there. It’s how she ended up sitting in a safe room while the kibbutz always told her that there are innocent, pathetic people across the border in Gaza and that only Hamas are the bad guys.
People moved there because the state sold very cheap houses after the discovery of the Hamas tunnels and the whole mess. The kibbutz filled up with new people; you couldn’t get a house there anymore. There was a 12-year waiting list. I was always scared about her living there; I was scared to go on visits. I was scared my daughters would be kidnapped from their home.”
The separation from Dafna was emotionally crushing. “It was very hard for me to wake up in the morning without her near me, with another woman washing my daughter’s clothes, without me cooking for her,” Maayan says. “We used to cook and do everything together. She’s everything I ever wanted. From the first moment, she met all the expectations I ever had, everything I’d dreamed my children would be like. Meanwhile, my financial situation deteriorated further. I was fired, and I collapsed. Since then, medication has been my companion. It’s keeping me alive.”
Then came the COVID-19 pandemic and, with it, the lockdowns. Maayan couldn’t find another job. A year and a half ago, she sent little Ella to live with her father on the kibbutz, too. The geographic separation from both daughters was emotionally harsh.
“I sometimes wanted to make some blintzes and bring them to the girls,” Maayan says. “I was afraid that all kinds of meaningful things would be happening to them without me beside them, like a first date or fights with friends. I was very busy with the parents’ committee at their school. They were my entire life.”
Maayan fought to maintain ties with her daughters, working to prove to them that they were the most precious things in her life and that she was a devoted mother, even if she couldn’t be with them daily as she was struggling just to survive.
She has recently been living in Rehovot, close to her older sister, after getting a job at Ben-Gurion International Airport. The girls would occasionally come to visit on weekends. Sometimes, she couldn’t even afford that. “I didn’t always have enough money to buy them food,” she says in a whisper.
The girls were supposed to be with her last weekend, but Maayan gave up her turn. The kibbutz was set to celebrate an anniversary in which they were to perform, so they stayed in Nahal Oz. On Saturday, Maayan was staying with friends in Tel Aviv and woke up to the sound of sirens blaring.
“I turned on the TV to see if there was an alert siren in Nahal Oz,” she says. “I saw that there was, and I wrote to Noam as usual, asking if they were in the safe room and if Ella was calm since she always gets really anxious during the alerts. He answered quite briefly that they were in the safe room and Ella was calm. The terrorists may already have been in the house. That was at 9:16. He didn’t answer after that.”
After a while, she saw on TV that terrorists had infiltrated communities along the border. She wrote to Dikla, Noam’s partner, as well as her two older children, in their 20s, who lived in other apartments on the kibbutz. Maayan shows me a video in which terrorists use Tomer, Dikla’s younger son, to try and convince people locked in their safe room in another house to come out.
The terrorist says that he has children, too, and promises the people inside the safe room that he won’t shoot if they come out. Finally, the family opened the safe room and came out. One of the daughters was murdered, and the father was kidnapped – along with Tomer.
When Maayan realized what was happening through reports on TV, she stopped trying to communicate or call, fearing the sound of ringing phones might accidentally reveal the location of families trying to hide. Her sister called shortly after 2 P.M., saying that Dafna and Ella had apparently been taken hostage.
“I didn’t know what she wanted from me, where she was coming up with it,” Maayan says. “She then sent me a photo my brother had found on Telegram, showing my two daughters sitting on a mattress in Gaza, wearing clothes I didn’t recognize with Arabic writing on them.
“I saw that Ella’s hand was wounded,” she continues. “When she first sent me the photo, I thought it was Photoshopped. I didn’t believe it was possible, since my family always blows things out of proportion. I preferred to believe it was Photoshopped.”
She contacted Dikla’s older son, who confirmed that videos taken in the family home by terrorists had been posted on Dikla’s Facebook page. He said they showed Noam shot in the leg, with Ella sitting on Dikla’s knees and Tomer held by the terrorists.
“You can see Dafna crying, and that Ella doesn’t understand what’s happening,” Maayan says. “After watching it a few times, I realized the two of them weren’t dressed, wearing only their pajamas. They were apparently snatched from their beds. You can see they changed their clothes in the photo from Gaza.”
Maayan went to her friend Iris’ house. She felt sure things would be resolved quickly. “I was sure they’d release them within a few hours,” she says. “I understood they’d been kidnapped, but I also didn’t believe it. I can’t explain it, I have no idea what I was thinking exactly.”
Before Maayan had even processed what had happened, she started giving interviews to foreign media outlets and anyone who wanted to hear her story. No official authority contacted her to explain what had happened.
“At first, I called the police to file a complaint” she says. “I tried several times. The policemen who answered said I was disrupting their work. I asked them what they were busy with if not the fate of my daughters. I then filed an official complaint with the police’s Lahav 433 national crime unit and gave them DNA samples.”
One day last week, she was interviewed by Oded Ben-Ami on Channel 12, displaying a photo of Ella as a baby, taken at some event with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, present. After the interview aired, she received a phone call from the prime minister’s wife.
“She promised to help me and said that Gal Hirsch and [former general] Effi Eitam would contact me. I told her I’d written Gal Hirsch and sent him the videos and photos, but he hadn’t responded. She said she would talk to them.”
Did any state official talk with you, other than Sara Netanyahu?
“When Oded Ben-Ami interviewed me, I met Zvi Tessler from the Home Front Command outside the studio. I told him it would be easier for me if they even just told me that they had nothing to report so far, if the state simply showed that it knows I exist and that my daughters aren’t here, that they’re somewhere in Gaza are in a dire situation. What matters is that they communicate with the families. I told him that we call and they don’t respond. I said that on air as well, and then people called me.”
Who did?
“Someone called me two hours after the interview aired. He said he was in the reserves and was there to assist me and would talk to me every day. Another officer called later, saying he would assist me. People from Military Intelligence called, too, asking that I send photos of my daughters. Everything was jumbled. I don’t need to be looked after; I need them to bring back my daughters.”
Did you get an official notice that they had been kidnapped?
“They told me I was in the best situation out of all the families of hostages because I had photos of my daughters [in Gaza]. Although no one had confirmed the photos were real, they showed the girls were in Gaza. I told them to at least check if they were Photoshopped images. I really want to know.”
Since last Saturday, Maayan has been living in a unit provided by a family in Kiryat Ono that volunteered to help victims of the border massacres. She doesn’t normally live near vulnerable areas that could be targeted in any case, but now prefers to be close to the center of the country. It’s where she can be close to places that might help resolve unanswered questions, with more access to journalists from around the world.
She also saw Noam, her former husband, in photos from Gaza. It appears that he was separated from his daughters and Dikla. Noam’s mother and Dikla’s family are also trying to raise international awareness of the kidnapping, speaking with any media outlet or public diplomacy organization willing to listen.
She’s in touch with some of Dikla’s relatives. “My daughters are very attached to Dikla and her family,” Maayan says. “She loves them, and they have a good relationship with her. She is a very strong woman, with a great presence.”
Maayan wants to get her picture taken in a batik dress Dafna made and with a mug that was a gift from Ella. She says she feels she’s with them this way.
“I worked hard to make the girls feel I was part of their lives, despite the obstacles,” she says. “Before they went to sleep, I played songs about children who are loved. I showed them the scars from the Caesarean section I had when they were born, telling them it was my best tattoo, that they were always with me, etched into my body. I’ve recently had a good phase with them, and it’s killing me that they’re there now, of all times. Do they wonder whether I love them, whether I’m trying hard to save them? It hurts me to think of the time together that we lost.”

TITLE: Arms airlift to Israel, bombers in Jordan, two carriers: U.S. deploying more forces to Mideast
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-16T16:32:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/security-aviation/2023-10-16/ty-article/airlift-to-israel-bombers-in-jordan-two-carriers-u-s-deploying-more-forces-to-mideast/0000018b-385d-d450-a3af-795de1010000

The Biden administration is deploying more offensive forces into the Middle East, to back Israel and attempt to deter Iran and Hezbollah from opening a second front on Israel’s north.
Last week, the United States deployed the aircraft carrier Gerald R. Ford and its strike group to the eastern Mediterranean. The USS Ford carries about 80 combat aircraft, electronic warfare and intelligence planes. It is accompanied by five advanced missile-guided ships, armed with Tomahawk cruise missiles capable of hitting targets inside Iran. According to satellite images, the USS Ford is about 180 kilometers south-west of Cyprus. P-8 maritime reconnaissance aircraft with anti-submarine, anti-ship capabilities are patrolling around the group.
The carrier strike group comes with sophisticated air defense systems that could make an important contribution to protecting Israel’s strategic facilities on sea and on land. Hezbollah is believed to have an arsenal of more than 100,000 rockets and missiles.
Over the weekend, a second carrier strike group, led by the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower, was dispatched to the Eastern Mediterranean and is due to arrive later this month.

Show more
The combination of U.S. and Israeli defense systems is not new. During the 1991 Gulf War, U.S. Patriot anti-missile teams arrived in Israel to intercept Scud missiles being fired at Israel by Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein. Since 2001, Israel and the U.S. have conducted periodic exercises in which they jointly undertake a range of interception scenarios and practice integrating the two countries’ different systems.
The U.S. fleet, if it is brought into action, will provide an additional layer of defense to Israel's (which includes Iron Dome, David's Sling, Patriots, the Arrow and the Arrow 3). Without a doubt, they will help a lot in the event that a second front opens against Hezbollah.
But by placing them off the coast of Lebanon, the U.S. is also giving itself a lever to restrain Israel if the Biden administration feels that its operations in Gaza or Lebanon are becoming excessive. There is a precedent for this two-pronged goal. During the Gulf War, the U.S. sent Patriots to Israel in exchange for Israel's agreement not to attack Iraq itself in response to the Scud fire. Washington believed that such a move might endanger the integrity of the international coalition the U.S. had created to oppose Iraq, which included Arab countries.
Since the Hamas attack on October 7, the U.S. has dispatched a large number of jets to the Middle East in order to “bolster the U.S. defense posture,” as the U.S Central Command has put it.
A squadron of U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle bombers based in Britain was deployed over the weekend at the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base east of the Jordanian capital of Amman. Another squadron of A-10 attack aircraft has also been deployed there.

Show more
An impressive airlift to Israel should be added to this list. According to online aviation tracking websites, at least 11 U.S. C-17 heavy-transport aircraft landed over the past 10 days at Israel's Ben Gurion airport and Israeli Air Force’s Nevatim base. Two of them were also used by Secretary of State Antony Blinken and U.S. Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin during their visits here.
In addition, an Israeli cargo plane made two flights to Dover Air Force Base in the U.S. According to an Israel Defense Forces spokesman, it carried "advanced ammunition designed to allow significant strikes and to prepare for additional scenarios." According to reports from the U.S., Washington has provided Israel with additional Iron Dome interceptors, advanced guided weaponry and bunker-busting bombs.
Watch: An Israeli cargo plane lands, delivering an initial shipment of advanced weaponry from the United States to Israel.
Six additional planes, operated on behalf of The U.S. Transportation Command, have also landed in Israel and are apparently being used to help to evacuate citizens and government employees and their families.
In addition to fighter and transport aircraft, two Rivet Joint reconnaissance aircraft belonging to the U.S. and British air forces have been operating off the coast of Israel in recent days. Coming from the U.S. and Britain, these are SIGINT (signal intelligence) aircraft used for gathering intel across the entire electromagnetic spectrum, including eavesdropping, geolocation and electronic warfare.

============================================================
TITLE: Israel evacuates citizens from Lebanon border as Gaza fighting enters 11th day
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-10-17T02:36:00+03:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-10-17/ty-article/israel-evacuates-citizens-from-lebanon-border-as-gaza-fighting-enters-11th-day/0000018b-3a30-dd09-a1bf-3ab8ba8c0000

The Israel Defense Forces and the Defense Ministry announced Monday that it will evacuate residents from 28 communities along the border with Lebanon, as the war against Hamas in the Gaza Strip entered its 10th day on Monday.
The merciless assault by Hamas on October 7 left over 1,300 Israelis slain and at least 3,968 wounded. At least 291 Israeli soldiers have been killed.
In the Strip, where at least 2,778 Palestinians have reportedly been killed and 9,938 wounded since the war began, Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad are holding hostage more than 199 soldiers and civilians, including foreign nationals.
The Knesset was forced twice to halt its first session since returning from a summer recess as rocket sirens sounded in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv and central Israel. Foreign diplomats present were forced to take shelter. A later bombardment on Tel Aviv happened during a meeting between U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who were forced to take shelter in a bunker.
On Israel’s northern front, tensions have escalated precipitously. Hezbollah has been firing anti-tank missiles at Israeli military targets, as well as an Israeli community near the Lebanon border.
According to the statement released by the IDF and the Defense Ministry, 28 communities within 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) of the border with Lebanon will be evacuated. The residents will be taken to hotels and guest houses that will be paid for by the government. The 28 communities are: Adamit, Arab al-Aramshe, Avivim, Bar’am, Betzet, Dafna, Dishon, Dovev, Ghajar, Hanita, Kfar Giladi, Ma’ayan Baruch, Malkia, Manara, Margaliot, Mattat, Metula, Misgav Am, Netu’a, Rosh Hanikra, Shlomi, Shomera, Shtula, Ya’ara, Yiftah, Yir’on, Yuval, and Zar’it.
Lebanese Prime Minister Najib Mikati was quoted as saying on Al-Jazeera that his country “is in the eye of the storm. The region is in a difficult situation and no one can predict what might happen.”
“The government continues internal and external contacts to maintain calm and distance Lebanon from the consequences of the ongoing war in Gaza,” Mikati added.
Talks have been conducted over the last days on a humanitarian deal to release some of the Israeli hostages being held by Hamas, foreign diplomatic sources say. At this point it isn’t clear whether such a deal can be reached and if so, what will be the timing.
“The work [on the deal] is ongoing and over the last days we have become more optimistic that it can be achieved,” said one of the sources.
An Israeli source refused to address the alleged talks or confirm whether Israel was directly or indirectly involved in them. Earlier, the Israel Defense Forces spokesperson said the army had updated the 199 families of the hostages on developments.
Israel's political leaders remained ambiguous on Sunday about how they intend to solve the hostage crisis. They spoke of “toppling the Hamas rule” and “removing the threat of terrorism to Israel,” while the cabinet sufficed with the noncommittal objective of exerting “maximum effort” to define the impending military operation.
The questions that are still pending are whether Israel will agree to a deal to exchange 36 Palestinian female security prisoners for some of the Israeli hostages, would Israel’s political leadership prefer a wide-ranging military operation against Hamas at the cost of harming hostages, or alternatively, would they prefer an operation that would attempt to rescue some of them.
The UN agency dedicated to Palestinian refugees said Monday that people claiming to be affiliated with Gaza’s Health Ministry seized fuel and medical equipment meant for humanitarian purposes from their compound in Gaza City.
However, approximately two hours after the announcement on X (formerly Twitter), UNRWA deleted the statement without specifying the reason. Sources familiar with the matter confirmed the incident involving Hamas and UNRWA, though the latter has yet to respond to Haaretz’s request for comment.
“Hamas stole fuel and medical equipment from UNRWA in Gaza. The amount of fuel stolen is enough to power Gaza’s water desalination facilities for six days,” the IDF said in a statement.
In their initial statement, UNRWA wrote, “Our staff were compelled to evacuate UNRWA headquarters in Gaza City on a few hours’ notice during the night of Friday 13 October. Since then, UNRWA has had no access to the compound and no additional details about the removal of the assets.”
They noted security cameras covering the compound’s entrance and exit were damaged in recent days due to the conflict and have not operated.
“UNRWA fuel and other types of material are kept for strictly humanitarian purposes - any other use is strongly condemned,” it added.
After the post was deleted, Israel’s Foreign Ministry account on X took a jab at the agency, writing, “Wait @UNRWA - Did Hamas also break into your Twitter account? Or are you just scared of disappointing your terrorist friends?”
UNRWA said Sunday it is no longer able to provide humanitarian assistance and warned that Gazans are running out of food, water and medicine.
Israel has allowed humanitarian aid to be delivered into Gaza from Egypt through the Rafah border crossing from Monday morning for a limited period of time. The supplies, which are being delivered by trucks under Egyptian supervision, consist mainly of water and medicines, but not food nor fuel.
Israel’s refusal to allow the entrance of fuel is said to be due to the fact that Hamas is using fuel intended for hospitals and citizens to operate its generators inside tunnels throughout the Strip.
Yaniv Kubovich, Ben Samuels, Jack Khoury, Jonathan Lis and Yael Friedson contributed to this report.

On unprecedented warzone visit to Israel, Biden faces a race against time
WASHINGTON – U.S. President Joe Biden will land in Israel on Wednesday for an unprecedented warzone visit that has already been cut short by the rapid escalation of violence in the region. Biden was forced to cut his itinerary in half before Air Force One could even leave the tarmac.
Biden’s visit, in word and deed, is designed to showcase America’s unwavering bipartisan support for Israel after the Hamas attack that led to the deadliest day in the country’s history — support that has been warmly and resoundingly welcomed by American Jews and Israelis from across the political spectrum.
