TITLE: Blinken makes forceful case for Gaza aid, says humanitarian pauses 'must be considered'
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-01T12:31:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-01/ty-article/blinken-makes-forceful-case-for-gaza-aid-says-humanitarian-pauses-must-be-considered/0000018b-8a38-ddfb-a78f-fe3bd45f0000

U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said that “humanitarian pauses” in Israel’s war with Hamas “must be considered” in order to allow supplies into the Gaza Strip and move civilians into safer locations.
“The flow of food, water, medicine, fuel and other essential humanitarian aid into Gaza must increase — immediately and significantly. It means Palestinian civilians must be able to stay out of harm’s way. It means every possible precaution must be taken to safeguard humanitarian sites. And it means humanitarian pauses must be considered for these purposes,” Blinken wrote in an Op-Ed published in the Washington Post Tuesday.
In the article, Blinken argued that it would be a “grave mistake” for the Biden administration to accede to calls from some members of Congress to withhold humanitarian assistance to Gaza civilians. Republicans in the House of Representatives had been making the case to cut all humanitarian Gaza aid out of the massive $106 billion emergency military and humanitarian funding package to Ukraine and Israel the White House has proposed.
Making a forceful case for including the aid to Gaza, Blinken wrote that withholding it “will deepen the suffering of more than 2 million Palestinian civilians — including women, children, the elderly, people with disabilities and other vulnerable populations — who have nothing to do with Hamas' deplorable attacks. It will undercut Israel’s security and regional stability. And it will worsen problems and risks that will end up costing American taxpayers many magnitudes more over time.”
“We don’t have to choose between defending Israel and aiding Palestinian civilians,” Blinken wrote. “We can and must do both. That is the only way to stand firmly by one of our closest allies, protect innocent lives, uphold the international rules of the road that ultimately benefit the American people, and preserve the sole viable path to lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians: two states for two peoples.”
Passing the full aid package, Blinken argued, “will show the United States’ unwavering resolve in standing with our allies and partners, standing up to autocrats and terrorists, and standing for an international order that safeguards America’s interests and values.”
He pointed to Israeli support for U.S. protection of and humanitarian assistance to Gazan civilians, saying that the Israelis acknowledge that these steps were “not only the right things for Israel to do — but they will also advance its long-term security. Israel’s leaders, he said, ”have made clear to President Biden and to members of Congress alike that they support the United States’ provision of humanitarian assistance to Gaza.”
Any U.S. aid, he vowed, would be subject to “rigorous monitoring and inspection measures to prevent the diversion of aid to Hamas or any other terrorist group. No humanitarian assistance is going into Gaza without first being inspected.”
Without a push for massive aid relief in Gaza, he noted, “the conflict is much more likely to spread, suffering will grow, and Hamas and its sponsors will benefit by fashioning themselves as saviors amid the very desperation they created.”
Such a situation, he argued, would “undermine the possibility of further integration between Israel and its neighbors” in what appeared to be a reference for the hope of normalization with Saudi Arabia - which had been on the diplomatic horizon before the October 7 attack. He also asserted that a “humanitarian catastrophe” would make it harder to “find partners” who “have a different vision for the future than Hamas — and who are willing to help make it real.”
Blinken also pointed out that, as it wages the war, that “the way Israel defends itself matters” and called on Israel to view Gazan as “victims” whose lives should be protected to the greatest extent possible.
Doing so, he conceded, “is difficult in any conflict, much less when confronting an enemy that cynically and monstrously uses civilians as human shields and launches rockets from hospitals, schools and residential buildings.”

TITLE: Widespread internet and phone services restored after major outages in Gaza
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-01T14:47:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-01/ty-article/widespread-internet-and-phone-services-restored-after-major-outages-in-gaza/0000018b-8a43-d466-a9ab-becbb74a0000

Communications have begun to be restored after Palestinians reported another widespread outage of internet and phone service in Gaza early Wednesday, hours after Israeli airstrikes leveled apartment buildings near Gaza City and as ground troops battled Hamas terrorists inside the besieged territory.
Palestinian telecoms company Paltel reported a “complete disruption” of internet and mobile phone services in Gaza, marking the second time residents were largely cut off from the world since the breakout of the war. Communications also went down over the weekend, as Israeli troops pushed into Gaza in larger numbers.
Humanitarian aid agencies have warned that such blackouts severely disrupt their work in an already dire situation in Gaza, where more than half of the population of 2.3 million Palestinians has been displaced and basic supplies are running low more than three weeks into the war triggered by Hamas' bloody October 7th rampage into southern Israel.
The International Committee of the Red Cross said the communication blackout would disrupt the work of first responders and make it harder for civilians to seek safety. “Even the potentially life-saving act of calling an ambulance becomes impossible," said Jessica Moussan, an ICRC spokesperson.
Last weekend, cellular and internet service abruptly vanished for most of Gaza amid a heavy Israeli bombardment. A rare few Palestinians with international SIM cards or satellite phones took it upon themselves to get the news out.
By Sunday morning, phone and internet communications had been restored to many people in Gaza, according to telecommunications providers in the area, Internet-access advocacy group NetBlocks.org and confirmation on the ground.
An estimated 800,000 Palestinians have fled south from Gaza City and other northern areas following Israeli orders to evacuate, but hundreds of thousands remain in the north, including many who left and later returned because Israel is also carrying out airstrikes in the south.
Gaza has been sealed off since the start of the war, causing shortages of food, water, medicine and fuel. Israel has allowed international aid groups to send more than 200 trucks carrying food and medicine to enter from Egypt over the past 10 days, but aid workers say it's not nearly enough.
Israel has barred fuel imports, leading to a blackout in the territory that relies heavily on generators for electricity. Hospitals have warned that their own generators may soon shut down, putting patients on life support at risk. Israel says it won’t allow fuel to enter because Hamas would confiscate it to use for military purposes.

God knows. In effect, after the disaster imposed on us by the Nazis (as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Hamas), maybe God has once again fallen asleep on his watch over the Chosen People.
U.S. sees Palestinian authority as possible solution in Gaza, yet Israel is working to weaken it
WASHINGTON – The United States and Israel are divided on the future of the Palestinian Authority. While the Biden administration is attempting to present it as an eventual governing body in Gaza, far-right members of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing coalition are working to weaken it.
The divide comes with the Americans increasingly wary about the status quo in the West Bank, where an already weakened PA on the verge of collapse and spiking settler violence threaten to destabilize the Middle East even further following Hamas' attack on October 7.
Analysis | Israeli army's faster-than-expected advance in Gaza makes its mission even more complex
The movement of IDF forces into the northern Gaza Strip was more rapid than could have been expected at first. Four days after the start of the ground maneuver, it is already escalating into a full-blown war, between IDF large infantry and armored forces, and the Hamas defensive array, which includes several concentric circles surrounding the organization’s security center in downtown Gaza. There is tough, persistent fighting deep in urban areas, much of them devastated in the air force’s preliminary bombings.

In 2018, Israeli big-data chipmaker Mellanox Technologies opened a development center in Gaza City. It continued operating even after the sale of the Israeli firm to U.S. corporation Nvidia in 2019, and continued to exist up to Hamas' October 7 attack on Israel.

The United States has been flying surveillance drones over Gaza in search of hostages taken by Hamas when the Palestinian militant group attacked Israel on October 7, two U.S. officials said on Thursday.

TITLE: Interactive map depicts scale of Hamas Oct 7 atrocities on Israeli-Gaza border communities
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-02T15:00:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-02/ty-article/interactive-map-depicts-scale-of-hamas-oct-7-atrocities-on-israeli-gaza-border-communities/0000018b-8fcf-d7a8-afcf-afef4f600000

Israel is still identifying the dead following last month’s attack on the Gaza border communities, in which around 1,400 people were murdered by Hamas memebers in the towns and cities surrounding the Gaza Strip, but enough information has come to light to allow Israelis to map out the extent of the catastrophe.
Some have taken this in the most literal way, producing an interactive online map showcasing every massacre site across the Gaza Envelope. The new website, “Mapping the Massacres,” allows users to click on every affected town and read a summary of what occurred there. Individual, color-coded, dots highlight the locations, on October 7, of Israelis who were killed or kidnapped during the attack.
While it is unclear who produced the map, it has been shared extensively online, including by government spokesman Eylon Levy, who said that he was unaware of its provenance.
Mapping the October 7 Massacre Key resource to understand the scale of Hamas's carnage. You can take it down to the resolution of the individual families massacred. oct7map.com
In an explanatory note on its website, the October 7th Geo-visualization Project said that it “strives to provide a comprehensive representation of the atrocities committed by Hamas” and that its map, which it described as an “educational tool,” was intended to promote “awareness of the gravity of the horrors.”
It cautioned, however, that due to incomplete information, its data “may contain inaccuracies or omissions, especially regarding location details, which might be refined as more concrete data becomes available.”
Fascinating visualisation and database, not by the @IDF or official entities, of the atrocities perpetrated by Hamas death squads on October 7th. Great resource for reporting. oct7map.com
The anonymous developers did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
When zoomed in, many of the towns along the Gaza border appear to be covered in red rashes from the dots indicating those who fell while a smaller number of black marks signify those taken by Hamas.
In its entry for Kibbutz Nahal Oz, where Haaretz reporter Amir Tibon hid for hours with his family as terrorists passed outside his house, the site noted that the town had been invaded by “roughly 100 Hamas terrorists…breaking into homes, massacring the residents of the kibbutz and wiping out entire families.”
A list of kidnapped and murdered Israelis, including a separate list for active-duty soldiers, followed. Clicking on a name brings up further information, including a photo, the victim’s age and/or rank and a link to press coverage of their death.
The map is a “key resource to understand the scale of Hamas's carnage,” Levy, the government spokesman, tweeted. “You can take it down to the resolution of the individual families massacred.”
IDF spokesman Jonathan Conricus likewise praised the project, tweeting that while it did not come from the Israeli army or any other official source, it was a “great resource for reporting.”

TITLE: TEVA is "all in" for schizophrenia patients
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-02T16:12:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/haaretz-labels/medica/2023-11-02/ty-article-labels/.premium/teva-is-all-in-for-schizophrenia-patients/0000018b-9051-d7a8-afcf-baf316bf0000

The large Teva site in Netanya (Abic) is home to one of the world's most advanced innovative-biological R&D centers. Owned by Israeli-global pharma-giant, Teva Pharmaceuticals Ltd., it employs some 400 people — 72 percent of them women and 98 percent with advanced academic degrees.
One of those women is Dr. Yael Marantz, head of the Teva Netanya site and Teva's vice president for non-clinical development. "In our site we are focused on developing innovative pharmaceuticals", she says, "that meet medical problems currently without adequate solutions or without any solutions at all." Innovative medications, she explains, may be built on substances so new they haven't yet been invented, or they may administer drugs in new ways that completely change how the disease is handled.
Creating innovative drugs requires vision
Discovery and development of such breakthrough medications take many years of R&D, testing and obtaining necessary approvals. But neither the decades of work nor the billions of dollars can guarantee a successful medication at the end. Deciding what to develop and on which field to focus is thus critical. "Teva has rich experience in drug development in areas such as central nervous system (CNS) disease, where we've repeatedly proven ourselves," says Dr. Marantz. "In our specialist areas, we've accumulated abundant experience in development and in marketing and sales, as well as establishing a range of academic collaborations, and deep knowledge of the surrounding technological ecosystem." Teva's focus on innovative drugs has already yielded promising results, with one of Teva's newest developments, a sustained-release subcutaneous injection for schizophrenia patients. The drug is given by injection once a month or once every two months, using an innovative administration technology. Most patients suffering from schizophrenia take medications that are taken orally and require daily intake. On the other hand, "our innovative development makes it possible to take this specific antipsychotic drug once a month or once every two months instead of daily, and this is a breakthrough that significantly reduces the risk of recurrent psychotic attacks", explains Dr. Marantz. "People who suffer from schizophrenia have great difficulty with Taking medication daily, and one of the most difficult problems in treating this disease is that the patients avoid or forget to take the medication and suffer from repeated attacks that greatly worsen their condition. The drug we developed can dramatically change the way the disease is treated." UZEDY for schizophrenia, which was only recently approved by the FDA and was developed in collaboration with MedinCell, recently joins a series of innovative drugs developed in recent years by Teva, such as Ajovy to prevent migraine attacks, Austedo to treat movement disorders caused by Huntington's disease or due to side effects of psychiatric drugs, and of course Copaxone for the treatment in multiple sclerosis and Azilact for Parkinson's, both developed in Israel together with the 'Weizmann Institute of Science' and the 'Technion' respectively. These days the company is working on a number of other intriguing developments, which are in advanced stages, for the treatment of inflammatory bowel diseases such as colitis and Crohn's, as well as another drug for schizophrenia.
Combining industry, technology and research
Of key importance in Teva's approach is its close collaboration with academia on one side and the hi-tech sector on the other. The company clearly understands that creation of innovative medications needs talented scientists, leading laboratories and the most advanced medical technologies. "Three years ago, we decided to align ourselves more closely with academia, and found dozens of laboratories in Israel with whom we could work," recounts Dr. Marantz. "Today, we're collaborating with the country's finest researchers in some 30 different projects, developing innovative drugs for CNS diseases, Cancer and immunotherapies. We're extremely proud of these academic and cross-industry collaborations. "Bio-Mix is one example of an inventive and fruitful partnership between Israeli academia and Teva. Each year, some 30 outstanding doctoral students are accepted into the project. Intensive mentoring, workshops and meetings nurture innovative, entrepreneurial, and innovative mindsets. Ideas sprout and blossom — such as a smart body-patch that warns of life-threatening allergy attacks, a drop of breast milk that identifies breast cancer, artificial intelligence (AI) that can diagnose disease early, and more.
The healing potential of AI
In 2021, supported by the Israel Innovation Authority and with venture capital funds and leading pharmaceutical and technology companies, Teva launched AION Labs with the purpose of transforming drug discovery and development. A global first, it brings together pharma, scientists, academia, technology leaders and investors — shattering the old model in which companies work in competitive secrecy. To solve the pharmaceutical industry's R&D challenges, it uses AI, cloud technologies and advanced computational tools — and the side benefits include reduction of animal experimentation and promotion of personalized medicine which places the patient at the center. Several startups have already launched from AION Labs. One of them is DenovAI. It combines advanced machine learning and computational biophysics to increase the probability of success for drug candidates, to find broader-scope antibodies faster and more economically, and to design from scratch complex potential antibodies that may become new biological drugs. Teva is also partnered Philips Healthcare in the seed-stage Sanara Ventures investment incubator fund. Together, they are investing in and supporting over 20 medical device and digital medicine startups. Teva is keenly aware that promoting medical innovation moves forward drug development more quickly and more successfully and can change the face of the entire ecosystem.
in collaboration with Teva

TITLE: U.S. official: Hamas tried to sneak fighters out of Gaza; Rockets fired on Tel Aviv, central Israel
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-03T06:04:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-03/ty-article-live/blinken-to-push-for-humanitarian-pause-as-israeli-army-encircles-gaza-city/0000018b-9334-db7e-af9b-fbf78ad50000

Updates
With U.S. backing, Israel and Ukraine discuss possible Zelenskyy visit
Israeli and Ukrainian officials have told Haaretz that the two countries are working on plans for a possible visit to Israel by Volodymyr Zelenskyy during the course of next week.
An Israeli official involved in the contacts says that the proposed visit has the backing of the United States, which seeks to present a united front of pro-American democracies fighting the Russian-Iranian axis.
58 Democratic lawmakers urge Blinken to push Israel for Gaza 'pause'
58 Democrats from both the Senate and House urged U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken to further push Israel on adopting humanitarian pauses in order to ensure sufficient flow of humanitarian aid.
The lawmakers, led by Sen. Martin Heinrich and Rep. Veronica Escobar, further pushed him to make clear that Israel must conduct military operations within the scope of international law and minimize civilian harm, as well as pressing Israel to prevent further settler violence.
They finally urged Blinken to lay the groundwork for intensive diplomacy efforts to achieve sustainable peace.
Hamas tried to sneak its fighters out of Gaza with wounded and foreign nationals, U.S. official says
A senior U.S. official said Hamas tried to sneak its fighters out of Gaza in ambulances via Rafah, delaying efforts to evacuate foreign nationals. Hamas provided Egypt and the U.S. with a list of those seriously wounded that it wanted to evacuate, along with the thousands of foreign nationals looking to leave.
U.S. and Egyptian officials found that a third of the names were Hamas fighters, none of whom were among the 76 wounded Palestinians eventually evacuated.
The release of two American hostages earlier this month from Gaza further serves as a "pilot" in ongoing negotiations aimed at securing other hostages, the official said.
"There's an active process going on here with multiple lines of effort," the official noted, describing it as "incredibly difficult, complex and time consuming."
Any arrangement would require "a fairly significant pause in hostilities," noted the official, echoing the Biden administration's support for humanitarian pauses.
The official further noted that Israel has "significant refined what originally was their plan" in terms of its military response in Gaza, adding that Hezbollah leader Hasan Nasrallah's speech did not signal "the beginning of a northern front or anything like that."
Brazil's Workers Party slams Israel for 'holding Brazilians in Gaza'
Brazil's ruling Workers Party criticized the Israeli government on Friday for not allowing 34 Brazilians to leave Gaza, saying Israel is playing favorites when deciding who should be allowed to evacuate the besieged Palestinian territory.
In three days since the Rafah border crossing between Gaza and Egypt opened to allow nationals of other countries to leave Gaza, Brazilians waiting to leave were not on the list approved by Israel, despite diplomatic efforts to include them.
"For the third time, the Israeli government denied the departure of Brazilian citizens threatened by the massacre against the civilian population in the Gaza strip," Workers Party president Gleisi Hoffmann said in a social media post.
She said the Israeli government has not provided any explanation for what she said was discrimination. Brazil tried to find a negotiated solution to the conflict when it presided over the U.N. Security Council in October, Hoffmann said.
"Unfortunately, the Israeli government signals that it has established a political hierarchy for the release of civilians, favoring some countries over others," Hoffmann said.
"We cannot allow that Brazilian civilians remain threatened in a region under military massacre," she added.
Brazilian officials said they have no explanation for the failure to let their citizens out of Gaza. Some local media have speculated it is due to positions taken by Brazil at the United Nations and comments by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
Lula has criticized the "terrorism" of Hamas that started the war, but he has also criticized Israel for its "insane" bombardment of Gaza that has killed hundreds of children.
Israel's UN envoy slams WHO for 'bias and double standards '
Israel Ambassador to the UN Gilad Erdan clashed with the World Health Organization, shortly after the international body criticized Israel's strike on an ambulance outside a Gaza hospital.
"Utterly shocked by reports of attacks on ambulances evacuating patients close to Al-Shifa hospital in Gaza, leading to deaths, injuries and damage. We reiterate: patients, health workers, facilities, and ambulances must be protected at all times. Always," said WHO Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.
Erdan responded that the WHO's "bias and double standards truly know no bounds."
"Are you on the ground yourself? Did you verify that Hamas terrorists weren’t exploiting the ambulance for terror? They did! You jump on any opportunity to condemn Israel, but remain absolutely silent while Hamas deliberately fires rockets at Barzilai Hospital in Ashkelon," Erdan said.
He continued: "Where was your 'utter shock' when Hamas Nazis murdered Magen David Adom paramedics while they were treating the wounded? Where were your calls to protect ambulances when Israeli EMTs were targeted by Hamas RPGs? Why is Israeli blood so cheap to you?"
IDF eliminates terror cell firing anti-tank missiles from Lebanese territory
The IDF says that an Israeli tank fired on a cell of terrorists that was attempting to fire anti-tank missiles from Lebanese territory into Israel. Israeli aircraft also attacked and killed a terrorist who approached the border area near the city of Shlomi, according to the military
Blinken, Gantz discuss 'efforts to maintain calm and stability in West Bank'
U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken told Israeli War Cabinet member Benny Gantz on Friday that "the United States supports Israel’s right to defend itself against terrorism consistent with international humanitarian law."
Meeting in Tel Aviv, Blinken and Gantz also discussed "ongoing efforts to secure the release of hostages and maintain calm and stability in the West Bank," according to a statement. Blinken also stressed that Washington "remains committed to advancing a two-state solution."
Berlin drops probe into police who removed Israeli hostage posters
The authorities in Berlin have dropped proceedings involving police officers who removed posters showing Israeli hostages held by Hamas, a public prosecutor's office spokesman said on Friday in response to a query.
The proceedings were discontinued due to a lack of reasonable doubt, he said.
Press law was not violated when the posters were put up, according to the authorities. Meanwhile, the police officers had also not damaged property, the authorities said.
Earlier in the week, there was outrage when it emerged that Berlin police had removed posters showing images of the Israeli hostages held in Gaza.
A video shared on Tuesday on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, showed officers removing the posters from an advertising pillar in the capital. The police said they suspected they were unauthorized.
In Berlin, some users on X criticized the police for removing the posters of the hostages and Berlin's police chief Barbara Slowik expressed her regret.
She could "absolutely empathize with the fact that feelings, especially of relatives and friends of the hostages as well as people in the Israeli/Jewish community, were hurt by the removal of the posters," she wrote Tuesday in a post on X.
Jordan says Gulf ministers, Egyptian foreign minister and Palestinians to meet Blinken on Saturday
Jordan said on Friday the kingdom will host on Saturday a meeting between U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken with his Saudi, Qatari, Emirati and Egyptian counterparts along with the participation of the Palestinians.

TITLE: Hezbollah's Nasrallah praises 'heroic' Oct 7 Hamas attack, says it was '100% Palestinian'
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-03T17:43:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-03/ty-article/hezbollahs-nasrallah-praises-heroic-oct-7-hamas-attack-says-it-was-100-palestinian/0000018b-95a4-db71-a7df-fded25b30000

Hassan Nasrallah, the leader of Hezbollah, said in a long-anticipated speech in Beirut on Friday that the decision to attack Israel on October 7 was "100 percent Palestinian" and that those who initiated "kept it hidden it from everyone."
Nasrallah opened his speech by saying the Israel-Hamas war, which he referred to as 'Al-Aqsa flood' – Hamas' officially term for the October 7 attack – has extended to more than one front. "We have already joined the battle since October 8," he said in his first official remarks since the war began.
The militant group's leader praised the "heroic" attack by Hamas, in which terrorists attacked farming villages and military posts in southern Israel, leading to the killing of more than 1,400 people in Israel.
“This great, large-scale operation was purely the result of Palestinian planning and implementation,” Nasrallah said, emphasizing that his militia had no part in the attack. “The great secrecy made this operation greatly successful.”
Nasrallah said the attack led to an "earthquake" in Israel. He added that one of the biggest mistakes Israel is currently making is setting goals which it "cannot achieve" – an apparent reference to Israeli leaders saying they hope to destroy Hamas' ability to govern in Gaza.
Further escalation along the Lebanese border between his group and Israel, Nasrallah said, is contingent on the escalation in the Gaza Strip. "We are ready for all possibilities," he emphasized, warning that "those who want to prevent a regional war must quickly stop the aggression in Gaza."
According to Nasrallah, Hezbollah's entry into the conflict forced Israel to keep large forces on alert on land, in the air and at sea on the northern border, instead of moving them to the West Bank or Gaza, and also led to evacuation of tens of thousands of Israelis from their homes in communities near the border.
Regarding the Israelis kidnapped by Hamas and being held in Gaza, Nasrallah said that Israel would only get them back "through negotiation."
He then said that Israel is committing "acts of genocide" and that "America is completely responsible for the current war in Gaza and Israel is just its tool."
Ahead of the speech on Thursday, a senior Hezbollah source said that the group simultaneously attacked 19 positions in Israel along its border with Lebanon. However, National Security Council Spokesperson John Kirby said that the U.S. hasn't seen "any indication" that Hezbollah is ready to "go in full force."
Also on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. officials believe that the Wagner paramilitary group, who has played a key role in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, may provide an anti-aircraft system to Hezbollah as a second front looms on the Israel-Lebanon border.

At a large demonstration in the U.S. capital Washington on Saturday, tens of thousands of marchers called for "Freedom for Palestine."

Celebrities such as actress Susan Sarandon and singer Macklemore also took part. Official police estimates of the number of participants were not initially available. After a rally in the afternoon, many demonstrators marched in front of the White House.
A journalist from the New York Post published a short video from the crowd on X, formerly Twitter, showing the demonstrators shaking the fence in front of the U.S. President's official residence and smearing the pillars of the fence gate with hand-prints in red paint. They were unable to gain access to the White House grounds.
The protest was organized by an alliance of civil rights and anti-war groups. Among the largely peaceful demonstrators, some stood out with placards referring to Biden as "Genocide Joe" because of his support for Israel. One speaker on stage incited the participants to chant with him: "It is right to rebel! Israel can go to hell!"
The Guardian: Approximately 1.5 million people in Gaza are displaced
The Guardian reported on Saturday that according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, about 1.5 million people in Gaza are internally displaced.
The report further stated that some 710,275 Gazans are sheltering in 149 UNRWA facilities, 122,000 are in hospitals, churches, and public buildings, 109,755 are in 89 non-UNRWA schools and the rest are residing with host families.
Palestinian news agency says dozens killed in IDF bombing of Gaza's Maghazi camp
The Palestinian news agency said overnight into Sunday that dozens were killed, mostly children and women, in an IDF bombing of Gaza's Maghazi camp.
Analysis | The U.S. is slowly and carefully drawing red lines for Israel on Gaza
WASHINGTON – Much ado has been made about U.S. President Joe Biden’s “bear hug” approach to Israel, both in general and in the aftermath of the October 7 Hamas attack, where he aims to use public support as leverage to privately pressure Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Whatever timeline Biden may have had in mind is rapidly slipping away from him amid rising international outrage, as the focus of the Israel-Gaza conflict is now primarily centered around Gaza's humanitarian crisis and no longer the October 7 attack.
The polarization is having stark effects at home, as well, as Israel becomes another political tool for Republicans, while Democrats continue to further drift in favor of a humanitarian pause.

The Guardian reported that 30 truck of humanitarian aid have entered the Gaza Strip on Saturday. 4 trucks contained medical supplies and medicines, while others delivered food, water, and other relief items.

TITLE: Turkey recalls ambassador to Israel for consultations; Erdogan 'erases' Netanyahu
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-04T17:48:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-04/ty-article/turkey-recalls-ambassador-to-israel-for-consultations-erdogan-erases-netanyahu/0000018b-9ad4-d27d-a9fb-dafd2f710000

Turkey announced on Saturday that it was recalling its ambassador to Israel, Sakir Ozkan Torunlar, for consultations, after Israel recalled its envoys to Turkey last month to reassess their ties following Erdogan's description of Hamas as freedom fighters.
In a statement, Turkey's foreign ministry said Torunlar was recalled "in view of the unfolding humanitarian tragedy in Gaza caused by the continuing attacks by Israel against civilians, and Israel's refusal of calls for ceasefire and continuous and unhindered flow of humanitarian aid."
Israel's Foreign Ministry issued a response on Saturday night, calling the decision to recall the ambassador "another step [of the Turkish president] to side with the terrorist organization Hamas." The statement added that "Hamas is the real enemy of the Palestinian people."
Israeli diplomats in Turkey had left the country before its foreign ministry recalled them, due to security concerns after pro-Palestinian protests erupted across the country.
Speaking to reporters on a return flight from Kazakhstan on Friday, Erdogan repeated his criticism of Western countries for their support of Israel, saying Ankara's trust in the European Union was "deeply shaken."
"Once all of this that is happening is finished, we want to see Gaza as a peaceful region that is a part of an independent Palestinian state, in line with 1967 borders, with territorial integrity, and with East Jerusalem as its capital," Erdogan was cited on Saturday as saying by broadcaster Haberturk and others.
"We will support formulas that will bring peace and calm to the region. We will not be supportive of plans that will further darken the lives of Palestinians, that will gradually erase them from the scene of history."
Erdogan said Turkey would support any initiatives to ensure that Israel is held accountable for what he described as war crimes and human rights violations, and that a failure to do so would erode trust in the global system.
He also said his intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin was in contact with Israeli and Palestinian authorities, as well as Hamas, but added that he would not regard Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – who Erdogan said was the sole perpetrator of the situation in Gaza - as a counterpart.
"Netanyahu cannot in any way be taken as a counterpart for us anymore. We have erased him, thrown him out," he said. "But otherwise, there can be no such thing as completely severing ties, especially not in international diplomacy," he was cited as saying by Haberturk.
Prior to the Israel-Hamas war, Turkey was working to repair relations with Israel after years of acrimony.
Erdogan added that Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi would visit Turkey at the end of November, and that he would attend an Organization for Islamic Cooperation (OIC) summit in Riyadh this month to discuss a ceasefire in Gaza.
Turkey, which has sharply escalated its criticism of Israel as the humanitarian crisis in Gaza has intensified, supports a two-state solution and hosts members of Hamas, which it does not view as a terrorist organization, unlike the U.S., Britain and others in the west. Turkey has called for an immediate ceasefire and offered to set up a system to guarantee it.
Erdogan said Gaza must be part of an independent, sovereign Palestinian state once the Israel-Hamas war is over, and Ankara will not support any plans "gradually erasing Palestinians" from history.

TITLE: U.S. and Arab partners disagree over need for ceasefire amid Israel-Gaza war
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-04T20:14:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-04/ty-article/u-s-and-arab-partners-disagree-over-need-for-ceasefire-amid-israel-gaza-war/0000018b-9b55-d8a6-a38b-dfd704630000

The United States and Arab partners disagreed Saturday on the need for an immediate ceasefire in the Gaza Strip as Israeli military strikes killed multiple civilians at a UN shelter and a hospital in a growing assault on the besieged enclave’s Hamas rulers.
U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken met with Arab foreign ministers in Jordan a day after talks in Israel with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who insisted there could be no temporary ceasefire until all hostages held by Hamas are released.
Jordan’s Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi said Arab countries want an immediate ceasefire, saying “the whole region is sinking in a sea of hatred that will define generations to come.”
Blinken, however, said “it is our view now that a ceasefire would simply leave Hamas in place, able to regroup and repeat what it did on Oct. 7.”
He said the U.S. believes humanitarian pauses can be critical in protecting civilians, getting aid in and getting foreign nationals out, "while still enabling Israel to achieve its objective, the defeat of Hamas.”
Senior Hamas official Osama Hamdan told reporters in Beirut that Blinken “should stop the aggression and should not come up with ideas that cannot be implemented.”
Egyptian officials said they and Qatar were proposing humanitarian pauses for six to 12 hours daily to allow aid in and casualties to be evacuated.
They were also asking for Israel to release a number of women and elderly prisoners in exchange for hostages held by Hamas, suggestions Israel seems unlikely to accept.
They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to brief the press on the discussions.
Israel has repeatedly demanded that northern Gaza’s 1.1 million residents flee south as it escalates the bombardment of the north. However, some of those traveling south were killed by Hamas in recent days, and Israel has continued bombing in the south, saying it is striking Hamas targets.
On Saturday, Israel offered a three-hour window for trapped residents to flee south, but an AP journalist on the road saw nobody coming from the north.
Israel asserted that Hamas “exploited” the window to move south and attack its forces. There was no immediate Hamas comment on that claim.
Some Palestinians said they didn’t go south for fear of Israeli bombardment.

They are sick monsters who slaughtered babies and chopped [off] heads. They raped I don’t know how many girls at that rave party. These things, I don’t see them echoed.”
The director, who is a devoted fan of the Liverpool football club, said he was disappointed by reports that at a mid-war match, Palestinian flags were allowed in while signs showing support for Israel were forbidden.
Folman wrote, produced and directed the acclaimed docudrama animated film “Waltz with Bashir” which won the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language film in 2008, and was nominated for an Academy Award in the same category.
The film portrays Folman’s struggle with the memories of his military service in the Lebanon War of 1982, through a series of animated reconstructions of real-life interviews Folman conducted with friends and fellow soldiers from the time, as he seeks to remember what his role was in the infamous Sabra and Shatila massacres: the killing spree by Christian militiamen in Palestinians refugee camps as Israeli forces stood by.
Folman, also the creator of the 2021 film “Where is Anne Frank?” spoke to the British newspaper about a new film project for which he is recording the testimonies of families of the 240 Israeli hostages kidnapped by Hamas on October 7 as part of the #BringThemHomeNow campaign lobbying for their return.
Thus far, Folman said, he has filmed approximately 70 people - with some of them receiving the devastating news that their loved ones' bodies were identified during his interview - transforming them from the families of hostages to the families of murdered victims.
Despite their situation, he said that there was willingness among the families to participate in the project.
“They want their word to be spread,” Folman said. “Also, I think for them talking about it is a therapeutic process they need to go through. Don’t forget that they were neglected by the government in that first week totally. No one talked to them. Total chaos.”

TITLE: A DIGITAL PRESENCE FOR EVERY BUSINESS: The maxshop Platform Brings Self-Service Technologies Under a Single R
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-06T10:49:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/haaretz-labels/2023-11-06/ty-article-labels/.premium/the-maxshop-platform-brings-self-service-technologies-under-a-single-roof/0000018b-a3ab-dc41-af9f-ebab3b5d0000

Businesses today, large and small, understand the importance a digital presence. They know that without it, their digital competitors will chip away at their market share and likely drive them into oblivion. Using the cloud for business needs, from mobile apps to online stores, has morphed from a luxury to a vital necessity.
More than this, a digital presence must be effective, especially financially. This was the vision of entrepreneur Oded Mesika in creating maxshop two years ago. A UI/UX designer, he has extensive experience in complex e-commerce projects and building software development methodologies, particularly mobile and end-customer experience. Today maxshop’s CTO, he is among 14 professionals there, with more to be recruited during the coming year. “E-commerce, which is essentially self-service consumption, is gaining momentum both in Israel and worldwide,” he explains.
“This trend demands a platform that creates better user and purchasing experiences for both business owner and end-customers.” Launched during the COVID pandemic, for maxshop the crisis was a growth opportunity. “Many businesses today find themselves dependent on website builders,” says Mesika. “But this not only consumes significant setup time and development costs, but also provides only partial solutions rather than a broad envelope.
maxShop’s fast, immediate and smart solutions go far beyond building a website or app. They’re part of a process that includes developing knowledge-rich technological solutions, which are regularly updated in the cloud, and address the needs and challenges of the business — from increasing sales to reducing costs. ”Among the range of its one-stop shop product-lines, maxshop emphasizes the mobile. The first and most advanced of these is its interface with POS cash register systems, which streamlines payment and shortens customer waiting-time.
It automatically generates reports according to different filters, enabling inventory management and smart decision-making in real time. And it provides customer data and purchase history for targeted, focused and customized marketing. Working in the cloud, it can connect to any of the company’s e-commerce platforms, allowing business operations to be controlled and monitored from a single cloud management interface. For companies that work with an external POS company, maxshop integrates their own product line — among examples are Aviv, Bikom, Caspit, Nike and Comex. A second maxshop product-line is an unmanned kiosk system, where orders can be placed around the clock — which is well suited to fast food, pharma and clothing chains.
“This increases business visibility, and thus helps attract new customers,” explains Mesika. “For the customer, it’s a quick, convenient and easy ordering experience, which offers the option of paying in cash, bills and coins, or by credit card, digital wallet, 10bis, Cibus, Goody or customer clubs.
”Smaller product-lines include tabletop tablets, in place of cardboard or paper menus, for ordering independently and reducing the waitstaff workload; QR codes and NFC tags that can be scanned when orders are placed via smartphone; the KDS kitchen management system with digital builders that reduce errors and costs; and digital cloud invoices that allow customers to ‘color’ their order. A third major maxshop product-line is currently under construction: it is an e-commerce site or virtual store, with full management interface independent of third parties, that can later control and add to the design without graphic knowledge.
What is the main market for maxshop’s online sales platform? 
“Our main market is any business that wants an online store,” says Mesika. “Our current focus is the fresh food market — that is, small supermarkets, greengrocers, farmers who market directly to consumers, butchers, restaurants and fast-food chains. Our platform can load hundreds of thousands of products at high speed.” 
What is unique about maxshop’s product lines?
“As I see it and from the very consistent feedback received from customers, maxshop is leading the self-service revolution because its sales platform is the most convenient, for both seller and buyer,” says Mesika. “We provide a 360-degree service package. Everything that a business needs in order to sell more and spend less is at maxshop. We’re a one-stop shop in the fullest sense. Among our services, customers can build a promotion system using tools in the system, such as Facebook and Instagram pixels, Google Analytics, Google Shopping, Instagram Catalog, Facebook Catalog and more. All of these are user-friendly, and none require prior technological knowledge, inventory management skills, advertising agencies or website promoters because they work automatically.” 
What types of business does maxshop target?
“Our platform is suitable for any retail business, from food and clothing through toys and cosmetics,” says Mesika. “We already have hundreds of signed-up customers — among them Optica Cohen, Katsefet, Pizza Fargo, Hashnizelia and Almost Free Pizza.”
maxshop builds different modules, according to customer requirements, he says, with the aim of making them accessible to micro, small, medium-sized and large businesses. “Studies we conducted have shown us that the majority of our market competitors provide only partial solutions. The few who offer full solutions use external suppliers, which inevitably harms the working of the different interfaces. This is why we emphasize all technologies under a single roof.”
What is the size of your target market?
“The global food market alone is expected to grow by 6.7 percent each year between 2022 and 2027,” answers Mesika. “This is reflected in Israel, where the annual growth forecast is 6.4 percent. Equally important, is the world market for restaurant management software, which is expected to increase by a very promising annual 15.8 percent between 2022 and 2030. Operating as we do in a very large market, both in Israel and abroad, these future growth rates guarantee our own growth. And, no less important to the market’s growth potential, some 70 of retailers worldwide believe digital transformation to be essential.”
International website: https://maxshop.io/ 
Israeli website: https://maxshop.co.il/ 
in collaboration with maxshop

SOURCE: haaretz

In a three-minute sketch broadcast over the weekend, the show leaned hard into criticism of pro-Palestinian progressives at the fictional “Columbia Unisemity,” based on New York’s Columbia University, with a pair of campus activists—one of them an apparently gender-fluid student wearing a pink keffiyeh—bragging about how their university is open to everyone on the LGBTQH spectrum. The H, one of the students explained, stood was Hamas.
“Yeah, I totally simp Hamas, it’s so trending right now,” the keffiyeh wearing student declared, before they both break out into a chant of “from the river to the sea, Palestine will be free” and begin denouncing “Zionist liars” for spreading “toxic” propaganda about the over 220 people held hostage by Hamas.
But despite their rhetoric, the keffiyeh wearing student declared, he’s “not antisemitic, I’m racist fluid.”
Going to split screen, the students then begin speaking with a Hamas gunman hiding in a tunnel underneath a Gaza hospital who declares that he needs more rockets, to which the student replies “as long as it’s organic.” But despite his enthusiastic support, the gunman seems unimpressed, inviting him to Gaza and promising to “throw you from the roof, you homosexual dirt.”
“Did you hear? They want to throw me a rooftop party,” the student responded in delight, shortly before breaking out into a new chant of “from the river to the sea, Palestine will be Jews-free."
Hostility to Israel has increased significantly on university campuses since Hamas’ October 7 attack, which left more than 1,400 people dead in southern Israel and prompted a massive Israeli military operation intended to root out the internationally-designated terrorist organization from the Gaza Strip.
Recent incidents include a pro-Palestinian mob storming a library at Cooper Union College while Jewish students took shelter behind locked doors, Jewish students at Cornell being ordered to stay locked in their rooms after a fellow student issued threats to murder, rape and maim them, and a student at Columbia suffering a broken finger after trying to prevent a person on campus from tearing down posters of Israelis taken hostage by Hamas.
Jewish students at Cooper Union are in the library as protestors pound on the door. Listen with sound on.
Columbia University has also come under intense criticism for an open letter signed by some 130 faculty members which described the October 7 massacre as a “military action” and expressed solidarity with students at the university who have been accused of antisemitism for suggesting that Hamas' actions are a legitimate form of resistance to “settler colonialism.”
Statements issued by student groups at elite institutions like Harvard and New York University in defense of Hamas have sparked particular outrage, with the president of the NYU Student Bar Association declaring her "unwavering and absolute solidarity with Palestinians in their resistance against oppression” in the wake of the attack.
At Stanford, Jewish students were reportedly asked by an instructor to move to the back of the classroom, so they would know what it felt like to be Palestinians. At Berkeley, students were offered extra credit for participating in a campus walkout against the “settler colonial occupation of Gaza.” And at George Washington University, a pro-Palestinian group projected the following messages on the library building: “Glory to the Martyrs” (an apparent reference to the Hamas terrorists who had murdered innocent Israelis) and “Divestment from Zionist Genocide Now.”
Israeli universities have reacted with outrage, criticizing their American counterparts for failing to adequately respond to declarations of solidarity with Hamas terrorists at their elite institutions.
Aside from lampooning hostile students, Eretz Nehederet has also gone after the foreign press, running a segment last week making fun of the BBC for its coverage of an explosion at Al-Ahli hospital in Gaza, which Israel, the United States and other governments attributed to a Palestinian rocket which fell short.
In the sketch, a BBC anchorwoman can be seen calling on her producers to change a chyron to show an increased death toll from the blast while an on-site correspondent declares that he is reporting from the “illegal colony of Tel Aviv” and presents obviously doctored footage showing a paper plane dropping Jewish stars on Gaza.
“We got this video from Hamas, the most credible terrorist organization in the world,” he declared, as the words “we love Hamas” appeared on the screen. The two journalists then move on to searching for a way to blame Israel for the bombing even after receiving word that Washington backed up Jerusalem’s account of the incident and begin engaging in conspiracies about Jewish foreknowledge of the 9/11 attacks.
“But it’s still Israel’s fault because the Israeli blockade prevented Hamas from getting proper functioning missiles,” the on-site reporter declared.
Israeli government spokespeople have harshly criticized the BBC for its coverage, accusing it of "regurgitating Hamas propaganda.”
The BBC issued a retraction about the hospital sham when it turned out the “Hamas-run health ministry” lied, but now it’s automatically regurgitating Hamas propaganda again, which it has not and cannot verify, like nothing happened. Lessons learned?
Reporting on the hospital incident, the BBC’s Jon Donnison stated that it was "hard to see what else this could be really, given the size of the explosion, other than an Israeli airstrike or several airstrikes.”
Last month, multiple BBC reporters were unofficially suspended following allegations that they had praised Hamas’ brutal attacks on Israel on social media, with multiple figures affiliated with its Arabic channel that the civilian victims shouldn’t be considered innocent civilians.

TITLE: 'I hope my kidnapped sister doesn’t give up, even though it has to be a nightmare'
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-06T14:42:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-06/ty-article-magazine/i-hope-my-kidnapped-sister-doesnt-give-up-even-though-it-has-to-be-a-nightmare/0000018b-a483-dc41-af9f-efa3f7c30000

Lea Yanai Mor and Lion Yanai are Moran Yanai’s big sister and brother. They both have families, homes and careers; both have moved from their hometown of Be’er Sheva in the south – Lea to Tel Aviv and Lion to a moshav in central Israel.
They call Moran “the little one” – she’s 40 but in recent photos she looks much younger. Moran never left Be'er Sheva, where she stayed to take care of their parents, who live apart. “Simply put, she’s the one who connects us all, who keeps the family together,” Lea says.
On Saturday October 7, Moran was at the rave near Kibbutz Re’im, selling her handmade jewelry at a stall. At 8 A.M. she called her father, screaming and crying in terror. “She said they could hear loud bangs and lots of gunshots, and that somebody was shooting at them,” Lea says. “Dad told her to get down on the ground; he didn’t really understand what was going on.
“At 8:30 my sister called again, to my mother, in total panic, crying and apologizing. She said she was afraid, that she was running for her life, that there were gunshots and her battery was running out. My mother didn’t know what to say.
“And that’s it. We were in complete shock. We wrote a thousand messages asking her to call us: ‘Moran, Morany, Moran, Morany, Moran, pick up, come on, pick up, where are you, where?’ But we didn’t hear anything from her. No matter what we did, we didn’t hear anything.”
Moran Stela Yanai, 40, from Be'er Sheva, southern Israel. Moran was kidnapped from the Nova Festival near Re'im on October 7. She went to the festival to sell jewelry she designs. Her family discovered a video showing her being taken by Palestinian terrorists after she tried to hide in a ditch. Moran takes care of her elderly parents, is vegan and loves animals.
Did you even know she was going to the party?
Lion: “Mom called her that morning because of the missiles. She didn’t even think about the party but she knew that Moran was in the Ashkelon area. It was only when they were talking that she realized she was at the party.”
 
Two friends who were with Moran got away and told the family what happened. “It takes time to realize that this kind of thing is happening to you, but they were resourceful and hid,” Lion says. “They somehow managed to slip into their car and tried to escape on the road. But the terrorists ambushed them, so they had to get out of the car, run into the open field and run as fast as they could. 
“They realized they had to split up; one ran into the bushes and my sister ran as fast as she could and was looking for a place to hide. I can’t imagine how she felt trying to escape like that. And that was the last thing we know about Moran – that they split up. It was Saturday at 9 A.M. This is the last evidence we have about her from an Israeli.
“A lot of people who know us, family and friends, helped us dig through the web and social media. Then on Sunday night we found a video on TikTok showing her being abducted by terrorists.”
Lea adds: “The video shows her in some kind of pit, begging for her life, and the terrorists who caught her say, ‘We caught a Jewish bitch.’”
There is no other evidence on Moran’s fate, but the family received a statement from the Israeli army informing them that Moran was believed to be a hostage. Since then, like most of the hostages’ families, the Yanais have been living in excruciating uncertainty.
“My parents, who are older people, have completely come apart. “They’re reliving it constantly,” Lea says, adding that she and Lion are trying to be as strong as they can for their parents.
“She’s the little one, the one who connects us all, so we need her. It’s so hard. We don’t work, we don’t eat, we barely function. But we’re full of purpose and asking everybody to do everything possible. ... We’re just thinking about the conditions they’re being held in, what they’re going through.
“It also strengthens my parents to see that we’re doing everything we can, going to the media, trying to gain a toehold wherever possible. We ask with all our hearts that everybody keep their eyes open, because time passes and it’s our human and moral duty not to forget, not to stop, to ask questions, to spread the word, to pray. Until they come back.”
More than anything, the Yanais are desperate for information that no one can provide at the moment. “The army sent somebody who deals with emotional resilience, but she didn’t have any information for us,” Lion says. “She’s a positive person and is trying to help my parents. But every time she comes over, they almost pass out. It’s a nice thing to help cope, but it’s not information.
“We’re also members of the Hostage and Missing Families Forum trying to take part in all kinds of activities there. The forum referred people to my parents, but they’re constantly in grief, they don’t have the emotional bandwidth to tell the story of what happened again and again. We’re here [speaking to Haaretz] in part to help them. We want to spread the message, especially internationally, and the request for help.”
Lea says the rave at Re’im was a self-exploration milestone for Moran. “She worked a whole year to start a jewelry business, jewelry that she designs with so much love. Her designs are linked to her love of nature, animals and different cultures. She really pushed herself forward this past year.
“At the party, she opened a pop-up table full of jewelry that she worked hard on – for her livelihood, for her independence. There are videos of her on the way to the party, and she looks so happy. We were happy for her and excited. She’s a wonderful person, full of love and compassion.”
Lea and Lion call Moran a free spirit – colorful, fond of jewelry and beautiful clothes, a vegan and an energetic animal-rescue activist. And in the past year she underwent some personal coaching.
“She was trying to get a deeper understanding of the difficulties of this world, to learn how to love herself and others,” Lea says. “She had a lot of hope, and this was light for us. I hope this light keeps her going. We believe in her and her strength. She also started writing poems; a very artistic person.”
For years the sisters’ relationship was more distant; Lea, now a ballet teacher after a career as a dancer, lived abroad. But recently the sisters have become very close. “She’s a very dear aunt to our children,” Lea says.
Segue into nightmare
Lion and his family were in London that Saturday; when they returned they learned that Moran had been abducted. “It was an extreme transition from a nice family experience to this nightmare,” he says.
“We chased every detail trying to get information. You constantly have to be focused and attentive, but you’re not alone. You see everybody’s grief. So you try to be prudent, not explode. But that’s inconceivable.”
What do you think should be done?
“We could appeal to the international community, to prime ministers, to people who can apply pressure, do things, whether it’s turning to Egypt, which helped with the humanitarian aid, to demand that the Red Cross at least visit the hostages – that somebody see what’s going on with them, give them medication.
“The hostages are helpless and they trust us to get them out of there. It’s a huge burden, more than is natural. And as time goes by, it’s not a day or two anymore. They say that Hamas sought humanitarian help in exchange for freeing the hostages, or asked for the release of Palestinian prisoners.”
Are you opposed to any of these things?
“We don’t know anything about any of this. We don’t have the time, and we’re on tenterhooks. I can’t tell the government how to act. I’m not a military man or a political man. But if there’s a suggestion from Hamas that will bring them home, let them do it as soon as possible.
“If I knew all the data, maybe I’d give you more answers. But I don’t have the resources to say what needs to be done. I just know how to turn to the government and say, ‘There are 200 families here, it touches the lives of all the people whose loved ones are over there. Bring them back as soon as possible.’”
Do you trust the government?
“All in all, the army and the authorities are people we’ve trusted in the past, regardless of our political opinions. I’m asking them to do their jobs, and we have to stand by them; we don’t have anybody else. I have to trust them. They’re my government, my country.
“They’re the organization I’m addressing, the organization responsible that has to give the answers about what’s happening with the hostages – because I can’t do it myself as an individual. I’m doing as much as I can to get them to buckle down. I want my sister to come home.
“That’s what matters most, and that’s what I’m focusing on. I don’t have time to become a political activist right now. We just don’t want people to forget. We won’t stop, but we feel that as time passes the pace is slowing. It’s not a new story anymore, there are no more shocking stories like in the beginning, it’s becoming routine.
“This lays heavy on us because it’s clear that if it’s not the first thing on the agenda, in the end, God forbid, it might become like the Ron Arad story,” Lion says, referring to the Israeli airman missing since 1986.
Lea says that before she goes to sleep she closes her eyes, pictures her sister and talks to her. “I see her maybe leaning a little on somebody there, maybe resting a little, even hugging a child. I picture her doing as well as I can picture it. I talk to her, and that’s how I fall asleep,” Lea says.
“I hope she finds a positive thing to hold onto and keep being strong, holding her head high. She has spiritual power. I hope she doesn’t give up, even though it has to be a nightmare.”

TITLE: Wildcats in Europe snubbed domestic cats for 2,000 years
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-06T18:00:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/science/2023-11-06/ty-article/wildcats-in-europe-snubbed-domestic-cats-for-2-000-years/0000018b-a516-d9c0-a5fb-ed5e1e760000

For about 2,000 years, wildcats and domestic cats cohabitated in Europe and Britain. Yet they did not interbreed, according to two new papers published simultaneously in Current Biology on Monday. The same applied to the Scottish wildcat – until the 1950s. Now the feral feline of the Highlands, the last wildcat in Britain, is in trouble.
The papers were based on genetic analyses of domestic cats and European wildcats, of which Scottish wildcats are a subset.
It turns out that despite living cheek to jowl for around 2,000 years, the domestic cat in Britain and Europe has at most 10 percent European wildcat ancestry.
That might surprise those who think they look pretty indistinguishable, and feel their pet is decidedly wild and undiscriminating when it comes to mate choice. It may seem all the stranger when one considers that the house cat arose from the Near Eastern wildcat, which is very similar to the European one.
But how much domestic cat do the wildcats have inside? In the case of the Scottish ones, rather too much, according to the paper published Monday in Current Biology by Jo Howard-McCombe of the University of Bristol and the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland, Mark Beaumont of Bristol et al. In fact, the Scottish wildcat could be considered genomically extinct: the study found not one single Scottish wildcat that retained the pure ancestral form. They were all hybrids.
Enter the Roman Legion
The cat that would become “domestic” joined human households commensurately with the mouse starting about 12,000 years ago – the time of the Neolithic revolution in the Near East – the archaeology indicates. We were charmed.
Who were these early cats? Recent genetic studies reveal that the house cats that have since taken over the world, all of them, descend from the Near Eastern Wildcat (Felis silvestris lybica) in the Fertile Crescent and Egypt.
The next stage in their world domination would involve cats walking with early farmers as they migrated out of the Near East and Anatolia. Although these migrants reached western Europe as much as 7,000 years ago, if not more, the ones to introduce the cat to the west and Britain were the Romans.
“The Romans really liked pet cats. They became a popular animal to have. As Roman culture spread throughout Europe, it became a thing to have,” explains Prof. Beaumont.
And as the domestic cats spread with the soldiers throughout Europe and Britain, they would meet the European Wildcat (Felis silvestris) and the Scottish wildcat, respectively.
One might have expected them to interbreed. Domesticated animals from pig to bee, chicken to sheep, readily mate with indigenous wild species. Boar-pig hybrids have proliferated, for instance, in the sealed-off area of the Fukushima power plant, where they are unmolested by the hunters among us.
Given that the wildcats and tabby cats seem very similar, wouldn’t they mate? Apparently not, which hadn’t been known before because of the paucity on genetic data on cats and wildcats, particularly Near Eastern wildcats. Despite 2,000 years of cohabitation, the domestic cats had less than 10 percent ancestry from European wildcats – though it varied, Beaumont says. Any given population of cats will have a different level of wildcat admixture.
As for the European wildcats, they had zero to little domestic cat ancestry, Alexandra Jamieson and colleagues report. The same had held true for the Scottish wildcat, which once thronged all England and Wales but went extinct there in the 18th century, and today exists nowhere outside Scotland – insofar as they do exist anymore.
The Scottish wildcats began intermixing with domestic moggies in the ’50s, as their own species became critically endangered. The domestic cats were the only game left in town.
Conserving who exactly?
Today, in the 21st century, the remaining wildcats’ Highland genomes are being swamped with domestic cat genes. “Eventually, through back crossing you’re going to end up with very little of the original Scottish wildcat genome,” Beaumont says.
Among wildcats living up to 10 years ago, some still had up to 95 percent of the Scottish wildcat genome. “In more recent [wildcats], it’s definitely diluted,” the professor says.
This is genetic swamping – where much of the ancestral wildcat genome is or will be essentially replaced, or mostly replaced, by domestic cat genes, through recurrent back crossing, Beaumont explains: “That’s usually going to ensue when one population is much bigger than the other. Domestic cats are swamping the wildcat in Scotland. There are probably only a few hundred Scottish wildcats left in Scotland.”
Hybridization of the increasingly rare wild animals around the world has created quite the conundrum for conservationists. Do you protect the hybrids, which effectively pose a threat to the pure species? The beleaguered Scottish wildcat, which looks like a tabby and is gradually becoming one, wants to know.
Theoretically, by selective breeding one could recreate a pure Scottish wildcat, as some people fantasize about recreating Neanderthals from the fragments of their genes in us humans. That’s beyond unlikely in either Neanderthals or wildcats, but there is a sincere conservation effort focusing on this small Highland feline: the Saving Wildcats project, which has gained some European Union funding, Beaumont says.
The aim: to reestablish the wildcat in suitable parts of Scotland, mainly in the Cairngorms, where there is a program to neuter free-range domestic cats. The project is based on a captive breeding program, never mind that there are no pure wildcats any more.
But at least the hybridized wildcats may enjoy some form of hybrid vigor. The Scottish wildcat turns out to have unexpectedly big chunks of domestic cat DNA that are involved with the immune system. Why is that?
Scottish wildcats exposed to domestic cats would catch their domestic diseases, and those who got immunity genes from domestic ancestors would be more likely to survive. But in the process, they also may have lost genes that were useful to them as wildcats.
Which brings us to why the European wildcat and the domestic cat didn’t interbreed until they had to. We don’t know. The researchers put it down to probably behavioral and ecological differences: wildcats are denizens of the forest and night. Domestic cats are denizens of our hearth and barns. And ne’er the twain did meet, until the wildcats basically had no choice.

TITLE: 'It's very personal': Inside Gaza with the Israeli soldiers whose lives changed on Oct. 7
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-06T19:21:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/podcasts/2023-11-06/ty-article-podcast/its-very-personal-inside-gaza-with-the-israeli-soldiers-whose-lives-changed-on-oct-7/0000018b-a559-d9c0-a5fb-ed59e9f20000

One of the first journalists to be embedded with forces in the Israeli army's ground operation in Gaza, Haaretz senior columnist Anshel Pfeffer shares his observations with Haaretz Weekly host Allison Kaplan Sommer after returning from a challenging battlefield.
Pfeffer, who accompanied a Givati infantry unit, describes the "really stark difference from when inside an armored vehicle you're using the screens, and in the next moment, you're outside, in the dirt."
He tells how the maze of tunnels under Gaza forces the soldiers to continually sweep the territory from every angle so "gunners and the commanders can constantly look at every point where they think a tunnel could open up and to try and spot it before it's used to launch a missile against them."
Pfeffer says that while the world is discussing exit strategies, humanitarian aid and conspiracy theories, the soldiers inside Gaza "really haven't been listening to the media discourses – the criticism of the government and the public relations war around the world. As far as they're concerned, their lives changed on October 7, they have been in this tense environment since."
He also addresses the "many convenient but very inaccurate comparisons" between the Russia-Ukraine war, which he also covered, and Israel's operation in Gaza, which is "totally different" both operationally and emotionally. While Russians ran away from serving in their war, he points to the highly motivated IDF soldiers who rushed to join in the fight after the atrocities of October 7.
"Many of them know people who were killed, who were taken hostage, or wounded. Some of them are from families which have been forced to leave their homes because of the war. It's very personal for everybody. There's no question about it."
While the soldiers on the ground "are very focused on their mission," Pfeffer says, "when you go up the IDF hierarchy to the top, there is a growing sense of frustration that there is no clear strategic idea of the next stage" once they successfully destroy Hamas military capabilities and potentially topple the regime.
"There is no real guidance or strategic idea of any kind coming over from this government, because this government is dysfunctional and has too many radical, far-right elements in it that refuse to even contemplate some type of Palestinian control of Gaza. And that is both frustrating for the generals planning this war, and also very damaging to Israel."

TITLE: German journalists detained by Israeli soldiers: 'Held us at gunpoint and asked if we were Jewish'
SOURCE: haaretz
DATE: 2023-11-06T20:04:00+02:00
URL: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2023-11-06/ty-article/german-journalists-detained-by-israeli-soldiers-asked-if-we-were-jewish-at-gunpoint/0000018b-a5ae-d9c0-a5fb-edfee9ed0000

Israeli soldiers in the West Bank threatened and detained a team of journalists from the German public broadcaster ARD, the network reported on Sunday evening.
ARD correspondent Jan-Christoph Kitzler was on his way back from an interview, accompanied by a Palestinian as well as a German network employee, when they were stopped by Israeli soldiers south of Hebron, according to ARD.
The soldiers behaved very aggressively towards the journalists and weapons were aimed into the team's vehicle on several occasions, ARD said.
A German Foreign Office spokeswoman on Monday demanded that Israeli forces grant press representatives free access for their reporting.
"In such a tense situation as we currently find ourselves, freedom of the press is of course an extremely valuable asset," she said on Monday in response to the incident.
Bayerischer Rundfunk (BR), the Bavarian regional ARD station that operates the network's Tel Aviv studio, described the incident as an attack on press freedom.
According to the report, the team of ARD journalists were on their way to report on violence by radical Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the West Bank.
"The soldiers threatened us with their weapons and asked us if we were Jewish. Our colleague was insulted as a traitor," said Kitzler, the ARD correspondent. He said the situation only eased after more than an hour, once other soldiers and police had been summoned.
Kitzler posted a photo of one of the soldiers with the face blurred out on X, the social media platform formerly known as Twitter, and wrote that "That's what might happen these days when one wants to report about the sharp increase in settler violence in the occupied West Bank in the shadow of the war in Gaza. Many of the soldiers there are themselves settlers. Journalists are likely not welcome."
Das kann einem in diesen Tagen passieren, wenn man über die stark angestiegene Siedlergewalt im besetzten #Westjordanland im Schatten des Krieges in #Gaza berichten will. Viele der Soldaten dort sind selbst Siedler. Journalisten sind eher nicht willkommen. #Israel
Show more
"The IDF [Israel Defense Forces] apologizes for any inconvenience caused," the Israeli army told dpa on Monday in response to questions about the incident. "The IDF will continue to act in order to ensure the freedom of the press in Judea and Samaria [the West Bank] even during the war."
The IDF also said that "the soldiers' actions were examined and protocols were reiterated," although the statement did not specify whether the IDF took issue with those actions or whether protocols were violated.
The Foreign Press Association in Israel in late October called on the Israeli military to ensure the safety of journalists and complained about two incidents in the West Bank in which soldiers had harassed reporters, including another incident in which ARD journalists were detained for two hours by soldiers while reporting on settler violence near Qawawis.
"This is the second incident in a week for us. Our team clearly identified itself as accredited press representatives and was far away from military security areas," said the head of the ARD's studio in Tel Aviv, Christian Limpert. "We cannot accept the actions of the Israeli military."
